2023013171.en_text: What can be learned about Scopus from the last two paragraphs?
2023013171.cn_text: 从最后两段可以了解到关于Scopus的什么信息?

2023013172.en_text: It fosters competition among citation providers.
2023013172.cn_text: 它促进引文提供者之间的竞争

2023013173.en_text: It has the capability to identify suspicious citations.
2023013173.cn_text: 它有能力识别可疑引用

2023013174.en_text: It hinders the growth of “international” journals.
2023013174.cn_text: 它阻碍「国际」期刊的发展

2023013175.en_text: It is established to prevent citation manipulation.
2023013175.cn_text: 它的建立旨在防止引用操纵

2023013176.en_text: What should an author do to deal with citation manipulators?
2023013176.cn_text: 作者应如何应对引用操纵者?

2023013181.en_text: This year marks the 150th anniversary of a series of Yellowstone photographs by the renowned landscape photographer William Henry Jackson.
2023013181.cn_text: 今年恰逢著名风景摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊拍摄的一系列黄石照片问世150周年。

2023013182.en_text: He captured the first-ever shots of iconic landmarks such as the Tetons, Old Faithful and the Colorado Rockies.
2023013182.cn_text: 他拍下了提顿山、老忠实泉和科罗拉多落基山脉等标志性景观的首批影像。

2023013183.en_text: Jackson snapped them on a late 19th-century expedition through the Yellowstone Basin that was conducted by the head of the U.S. Geological and Geographical Survey of the Territories, Ferdinand V. Hayden.
2023013183.cn_text: 这些照片是杰克逊在19世纪晚期一次穿越黄石盆地的探险中拍摄的，该探险由美国领土地质与地理调查局局长费迪南德·V·海登率领。

2023013186.en_text: The team included a meteorologist, a zoologist, a mineralogist, and an agricultural statistician.
2023013186.cn_text: 团队成员还包括一名气象学家、一名动物学家、一名矿物学家和一名农业统计学家。

2023013187.en_text: Two centuries ago, the idea of preserving nature, rather than exploiting it, was a novel one to many U.S. settlers.
2023013187.cn_text: 两个世纪前，对许多美国定居者而言，「保护自然而非开发自然」的理念还是十分新颖的想法。

2023013188.en_text: One of the turning points in public support for land conservation efforts — and recognizing the magnificence of the Yellowstone region in particular — came in the form of vivid photographs.
2023013188.cn_text: 而促使公众转而支持土地保护事业——尤其是认识到黄石地区之壮美——的转折点之一，正是这些生动的照片。

2023013189.en_text: As an effective Washington operator, Hayden sensed that he could capitalize on the expedition’s stunning visuals.
2023013189.cn_text: 作为一名精于运作的华盛顿人士，海登意识到自己可以借助此次探险中令人震撼的视觉影像。

2023013190.en_text: He asked Jackson to print out large copies and distributed them, along with reproductions of Moran’s paintings, to each member of Congress.
2023013190.cn_text: 他让杰克逊冲印出大幅照片，连同莫兰的画作复制品一并分发给每一位国会议员。

2023013191.en_text: “The visualization, particularly those photographs, really hit home that this is something that has to be protected,” says Murphy.
2023013191.cn_text: “这些视觉影像，尤其是那些照片，真正让人切身感受到这是必须加以保护的地方，”墨菲说道。

2023013192.en_text: Throughout the trip, Jackson juggled multiple cameras and plate sizes using the “collodion process” that required him to coat the plates with a chemical mixture, then expose them and develop the resulting images with a portable darkroom.
2023013192.cn_text: 旅途中，杰克逊借助“湿版摄影法”同时操作多台相机及不同尺寸的底片，这种方法需要先在底片上涂覆化学药剂，再进行曝光，并在便携暗房中显影成像。

2023013193.en_text: The crude technique required educated guesses on exposure times, and involved heavy, awkward equipment — several men had to assist in its transportation.
2023013193.cn_text: 这种原始的技术要求凭经验估算曝光时间，且所用设备笨重不便，须由数人合力搬运。

2023013194.en_text: Despite these challenges, Jackson captured dozens of striking photos, ranging from majestic images like his now-famous snapshot of Old Faithful, to casual portraits of expedition members at the camp.
2023013194.cn_text: 尽管困难重重，杰克逊仍拍下了数十张令人惊叹的照片，既有他那张如今已声名远扬的老忠实泉快照那样气势恢宏的画面，也有探险队员们在营地的随性肖像。

2023013195.en_text: While veterans of previous expeditions wrote at length about stunning trail sights, these vivid photographs were another thing entirely.
2023013195.cn_text: 以往探险的老手们虽曾在文字中细述沿途壮丽景色，但这些生动的照片带来的却是截然不同的震撼。

2023013196.en_text: The journey officially began in Ogden, Utah on June 8, 1871.
2023013196.cn_text: 此次旅程于1871年6月8日在犹他州奥格登正式启程。

2023013197.en_text: Over nearly four months, dozens of men made their way on horseback into Montana and traversed along the Yellowstone River and around Yellowstone Lake.
2023013197.cn_text: 在将近四个月的时间里，数十人骑马进入蒙大拿州，沿黄石河及黄石湖周边一路跋涉。

2023013198.en_text: That fall, they concluded the survey in Fort Bridger, Wyoming.
2023013198.cn_text: 当年秋天，他们在怀俄明州的布里杰堡结束了此次考察。

2023013199.en_text: Though Native Americans (and later miners and fur trappers) had long recognized the area’s riches, most Americans did not.
2023013199.cn_text: 尽管美洲原住民（以及后来的矿工与毛皮猎人）早已认识到该地区物产丰饶，但大多数美国人对此却一无所知。

2023013200.en_text: That’s why Hayden’s expedition aimed to produce a fuller understanding of the Yellowstone River region, from its hot springs and waterfalls to its variety of flora and fauna.
2023013200.cn_text: 正因如此，海登的探险队旨在更全面地认识黄石河地区——从温泉、瀑布到各类动植物，无所不包。

2023013201.en_text: In addition to the entourage of scientists, the team also included artists: Painter Thomas Moran and photographer William Henry Jackson were charged with capturing this astounding natural beauty and sharing it with the world.
2023013201.cn_text: 随行人员除了科学家之外，还有艺术家：画家托马斯·莫兰与摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊肩负着记录这一惊人自然美景并将其展示给世人的使命。

2023013202.en_text: The bill proved largely popular and sailed through Congress with large majorities in favor.
2023013202.cn_text: 该法案获得广泛支持，在国会以压倒性多数顺利通过。

2023013203.en_text: In quick succession, the Senate and House passed legislation protecting Yellowstone in early 1872.
2023013203.cn_text: 1872年初，参众两院相继通过了保护黄石地区的立法。

2023013204.en_text: That March, President Ulysses S. Grant signed an act into law that established Yellowstone as the world’s first national park.
2023013204.cn_text: 同年三月，总统尤利西斯·S·格兰特签署法案，正式将黄石设立为世界上第一座国家公园。

2023013206.en_text: While some locals opposed to the designation, the decision was largely accepted — and Jackson’s photos played a key role in the fight to protect the area.
2023013206.cn_text: 虽有部分当地居民反对这一指定，但这一决定总体上仍被广泛接受——而杰克逊的照片在这场保护该地区的斗争中发挥了关键作用。

2023013207.en_text: “I don’t believe that the legal protection would have happened in the timeframe that it did without those images,” says Heather Hansen, journalist and author of Prophets and Moguls, Rangers and Rogues, Bison and Bears:100 Years of the National Park Service.
2023013207.cn_text: “我认为，若没有那些影像，法律保护恐怕不会在那样的时间内得以实现，”记者兼《先知与巨头，护林员与流氓，野牛与熊：国家公园管理局百年史》一书作者希瑟·汉森如是说。

2023013208.en_text: Perhaps most importantly, the images provided documentary evidence of the park’s sights that later made its way to government officials.
2023013208.cn_text: 也许最为重要的是，这些影像为公园景观提供了实证记录，并最终呈送到政府官员手中。

2023013209.en_text: Weeks after completing the expedition, Hayden collected his team’s observations into an extensive report aimed at convincing senators and representatives, along with colleagues at government agencies like the Department of the Interior, that Yellowstone ought to be preserved.
2023013209.cn_text: 探险结束数周后，海登将团队的观察所得汇编成一份详尽的报告，力图说服参众两院议员，以及内政部等政府机构的同僚，让他们相信黄石理应得到保护。

2023013215.en_text: There has been some exploration around the use of AI in digital marketing.
2023013215.cn_text: 围绕人工智能在数字营销中的应用已经开展了一些探索。

2023013216.en_text: For example, AI can be used to analyse what type of advertising content or copy would be appropriate to ‘speak’ to a specific target customer group by revealing information about trends and preferences through the analysis of big data.
2023013216.cn_text: 例如，人工智能可以通过分析大数据来揭示趋势和偏好信息，从而分析哪种类型的广告内容或文案适合与特定目标客户群体「对话」。

2023013217.en_text: AI can also be used to identify the lifestyle choices of customers regarding their hobbies, favourite celebrities, music choices, and fashions to provide unique content in marketing messages put out through social media.
2023013217.cn_text: 人工智能还可以用于识别客户在爱好、喜爱的名人、音乐选择和时尚方面的生活方式选择，从而在通过社交媒体发布的营销信息中提供独特的内容。

2023013218.en_text: At the same time AI can also be used to generate content for social media posts and chat sites.
2023013218.cn_text: 与此同时，人工智能还可以用于为社交媒体帖子和聊天网站生成内容。

2023013219.en_text: AI can also provide a bridge between the need of the brand to communicate emotionally with the customer and identifying their rapidly changing needs.
2023013219.cn_text: 人工智能还可以在品牌与客户进行情感沟通的需求和识别客户快速变化的需求之间搭建桥梁。

2023013220.en_text: The main disadvantage of using AI to respond to customers is that there are concerns about trusting personal interactions to machines, which could lead not only to the subsequent loss of interpersonal connections, but also to a decrease in marketing personnel.
2023013220.cn_text: 使用人工智能回应客户的主要缺点在于，人们对将个人互动托付给机器存在信任方面的担忧，这不仅可能导致人际联系的随之丧失，还可能导致营销人员的减少。

2023013221.en_text: Some believe that AI is negatively impacting on the marketer’s role by reducing creativity and removing jobs, but they are aware that it is a way of reducing costs and creating new information.
2023013221.cn_text: 一些人认为，人工智能通过降低创造力和减少工作岗位，对营销人员的角色产生了负面影响，但他们也意识到这是一种降低成本和创造新信息的方式。

2023013222.en_text: By allowing AI to develop content some brand marketers may find that they are losing control over the brand narrative.
2023013222.cn_text: 通过让人工智能开发内容，一些品牌营销人员可能会发现他们正在失去对品牌叙事的控制。

2023013223.en_text: Algorithms that are used to simulate human interactions are creating many of these concerns, especially as no-one is quite sure what the outcomes of using AI to interact with customers will be.
2023013223.cn_text: 用于模拟人类互动的算法正在引发许多此类担忧,尤其是因为没有人完全确定使用人工智能与客户互动的结果将会如何。

2023013224.en_text: For AI to be successful, data needs to be accessible, but the use of personal data is becoming more regulated and the automated sharing of data is becoming more difficult.
2023013224.cn_text: 要让人工智能取得成功，数据需要是可访问的，但个人数据的使用正变得更加受到监管，数据的自动共享也变得更加困难。

2023013225.en_text: If customers are not willing to share data, AI will be starved of essential information and will not be able to function effectively or employ machine learning to improve its marketing content and communication.
2023013225.cn_text: 如果客户不愿意共享数据，人工智能将缺乏必要的信息，无法有效运作或利用机器学习来改进其营销内容和沟通方式。

2023013226.en_text: Therefore, unless customers are prepared to sign release agreements, the use of AI may become somewhat restricted in the future.
2023013226.cn_text: 因此，除非客户愿意签署授权协议，否则人工智能的使用在未来可能会受到某种程度的限制。

2023013227.en_text: Not only can AI help to create the marketing content, but it can also provide a non-intrusive way of delivering the content to the target customers.
2023013227.cn_text: 人工智能不仅可以帮助创建营销内容，还可以提供一种非侵扰性的方式将内容传递给目标客户。

2023013228.en_text: Data can be gathered on where the customer can be engaged, such as location, devices used, website interactions, and sites visited, to display marketing messages in appropriate forms, including emails, social media posts, pop-up advertisements, and banners at an appropriate frequency.
2023013228.cn_text: 可以收集关于客户可以被触达的位置的数据，例如地理位置、使用的设备、网站互动和访问过的网站，以便以适当的形式和适当的频率展示营销信息，包括电子邮件、社交媒体帖子、弹出式广告和横幅广告。

2023013229.en_text: The non-intrusive delivery of the marketing messages in a way that is sensitive to the needs of the target customer is one of the critical challenges to the digital marketer.
2023013229.cn_text: 以一种对目标客户需求敏感的方式非侵扰性地传递营销信息，是数字营销人员面临的关键挑战之一。

2023013230.en_text: Understanding humans may be complicated, but we reveal a considerable amount about what appeals to us through our browsing history.
2023013230.cn_text: 理解人类可能很复杂，但我们通过浏览历史揭示了大量关于什么能吸引我们的信息。

2024013001.en_text: There’s nothing more welcoming than a door opening for you.
2024013001.cn_text: 没有什么比一扇为你敞开的门更让人感到受欢迎了。

2024013002.en_text: Without the need to be touched to open or close, automatic doors are essential in improving disabled access to buildings and helping provide general convenience to commercial buildings.
2024013002.cn_text: 自动门无需触碰即可开闭，在改善残障人士建筑通行条件、为商业建筑提供整体便利方面不可或缺。

2024013003.en_text: Self-sliding doors began to emerge as a commercial product in 1960 after being invented six years previously by Americans Dee Horton and Lew Hewitt.
2024013003.cn_text: 自动滑门于1960年开始作为商品投入市场,此前六年由美国人迪·霍顿和卢·休伊特发明。

2024013004.en_text: They started out as a novelty feature, but as their use has grown, their benefits have extended within our technologically advanced world.
2024013004.cn_text: 它们最初作为新奇功能出现,但随着使用范围的扩大,其效用在我们这个技术发达的世界中得到了延伸。

2024013005.en_text: Particularly useful in busy locations or during times of emergency, the doors act as crowd management by reducing the obstacles put in people’s way.
2024013005.cn_text: 在人流密集场所或紧急时刻,这些门通过减少通行障碍发挥人群疏导作用,尤为实用。

2024013006.en_text: As well as making access both in and out of buildings easier for people, the difference in the way many of these doors open helps reduce the total area occupied by them.
2024013006.cn_text: 除了使人们进出建筑更加便利,许多此类门的开启方式差异还有助于减少其占用的总面积。

2024013007.en_text: Automatic doors often open to the side, with the panels sliding across one another.
2024013007.cn_text: 自动门通常横向开启,门扇相互滑动。

2024013008.en_text: Replacing swing doors, these allow smaller buildings to maximise the usable space inside without having to clear the way for a large, sticking-out door.
2024013008.cn_text: 这类门取代了平开门,使小型建筑能够最大化利用内部空间,无需为突出的大型门扇预留通道。

2024013009.en_text: There are many different types of automatic door, with each relying on specific signals to tell them when to open.
2024013009.cn_text: 自动门种类繁多,每种都依靠特定信号来判断开启时机。

2024013010.en_text: Although these methods differ, the main principles remain the same.
2024013010.cn_text: 尽管方法各异,但基本原理相同。

2024013011.en_text: Each automatic door system analyses the light, sound, weight or movement in their vicinity as a signal to open.
2024013011.cn_text: 每套自动门系统都通过分析周围的光、声、重量或运动来获取开启信号。

2024013012.en_text: Sensor types are chosen to complement the different environments they are needed in.
2024013012.cn_text: 传感器类型的选择要与其所处的不同环境相适应。

2024013013.en_text: For example, a busy street might not suit a motion-sensored door, as it would constantly be opening for passers-by.
2024013013.cn_text: 例如,繁忙街道可能不适合使用动作感应门,因为它会不断为过往行人开启。

2024013014.en_text: A pressure-sensitive mat would be more appropriate to limit the surveyed area.
2024013014.cn_text: 压力感应垫更适合用于限定监测范围。

2024013015.en_text: Nearly 2,000 years ago, as the Romans began to pull out of Scotland, they left behind a curious treasure: 10 tons of nails, nearly a million of the things.
2024013015.cn_text: 大约2000年前,当罗马人开始撤离苏格兰时,他们留下了一件奇特的宝藏:10吨钉子,近百万枚之多。

2024013016.en_text: The nail hoard was discovered in 1960 in a four-metre-deep pit covered by two metres of gravel.
2024013016.cn_text: 这批钉子藏品于1960年被发现,位于一个四米深的坑中,上面覆盖着两米厚的砾石。

2024013017.en_text: Why had the Romans buried a million nails?
2024013017.cn_text: 罗马人为何要埋藏百万枚钉子?

2024013018.en_text: The likely explanation is that the withdrawal was rushed, and they didn’t want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapon-grade iron.
2024013018.cn_text: 最可能的解释是撤退过于仓促,他们不想让当地喀里多尼亚人获得10吨武器级铁材。

2024013019.en_text: The Romans buried the nails so deep that they would not be discovered for almost two millennia.
2024013019.cn_text: 罗马人将钉子埋得极深,以至于近两千年都未被发现。

2024013020.en_text: Later civilisations would value the skilled blacksmith’s labour in a nail even more than the raw material.
2024013020.cn_text: 后世文明对一枚钉子中熟练铁匠劳动的重视,甚至超过了对原材料本身的重视。

2024013021.en_text: As Roma Agrawal explains in her new delightful book Nuts and Bolts, early 17th-century Virginians would sometimes burn down their homes if they were planning to relocate.
2024013021.cn_text: 正如罗玛·阿格拉瓦尔在其新作《螺母与螺栓》中所解释的,17世纪早期的弗吉尼亚人在计划搬迁时有时会烧毁自己的房屋。

2024013022.en_text: This was an attempt to recover the valuable nails, which could be reused after sifting the ashes.
2024013022.cn_text: 这是为了回收有价值的钉子,这些钉子在筛过灰烬后可以重新使用。

2024013023.en_text: The idea that one might burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was.
2024013023.cn_text: 仅为回收钉子而烧毁整座房屋的做法,凸显了这种看似简单的技术是多么稀缺、昂贵且珍贵。

2024013024.en_text: The price of nails fell by 90% between the late 1700s and mid-1900s, as economist Daniel Sichel points out in a research paper.
2024013024.cn_text: 正如经济学家丹尼尔·西切尔在一篇研究论文中指出的,从18世纪末到20世纪中期,钉子的价格下降了90%。

2024013025.en_text: According to Sichel, although the falling price of nails was driven partly by cheaper iron and cheaper energy, most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails.
2024013025.cn_text: 根据西切尔的研究,虽然钉子价格的下降部分源于铁材和能源成本的降低,但主要归功于钉子制造商找到了更高效的方式将钢材制成钉子。

2024013026.en_text: Nails themselves have changed over the years, but Sichel studied them because they haven’t changed much.
2024013026.cn_text: 钉子本身多年来有所变化,但西切尔研究它们正是因为它们变化不大。

2024013027.en_text: Roman lamps and Roman chariots are very different from LED strips and sports cars, but Roman nails are still clearly nails.
2024013027.cn_text: 罗马灯与LED灯条、罗马战车与跑车大相径庭,但罗马钉与现代钉显然仍是同一种东西。

2024013028.en_text: It would be absurd to try to track the changing price of sports cars since 1695, but to ask the same question of nails makes perfect sense.
2024013028.cn_text: 试图追踪自1695年以来跑车价格的变化是荒谬的,但对钉子提出同样的问题却完全合理。

2024013029.en_text: I make no apology for being obsessed by a particular feature of these objects: their price.
2024013029.cn_text: 我对这些物品的某一特定特征——它们的价格——十分着迷,对此我毫不抱歉。

2024013030.en_text: I am an economist, after all.

2024013031.en_text: After writing two books about the history of inventions, one thing I’ve learnt is that while it is the enchantingly sophisticated technologies that get all the hype, it’s the cheap technologies that change the world.
2024013031.cn_text: 在撰写两本关于发明史的著作后,我明白了一件事:尽管那些极为精密的技术吸引了所有关注,但真正改变世界的是廉价技术。

2024013032.en_text: The Gutenberg printing press transformed civilisation not by changing the nature of writing but by changing its cost — and it would have achieved little without a parallel collapse in the price of surfaces to write on, thanks to an often-overlooked technology called paper.
2024013032.cn_text: 古腾堡印刷机改变文明,并非通过改变书写的性质,而是通过改变其成本——而且若非一种常被忽视的技术即纸张令书写表面的价格同步下降,它也难有大的成就。

2024013033.en_text: Solar panels had few niche uses until they became cheap; now they are transforming the global energy system.
2024013033.cn_text: 太阳能板在价格变得低廉之前用途有限;如今它们正在改变全球能源体系。

2024013059.en_text: Parenting tips obtained from hunter-gatherers in Africa may be the key to bringing up more contented children, researchers have suggested.
2024013059.cn_text: 研究人员提出，从非洲狩猎采集者那里获得的育儿经验可能是培养更快乐孩子的关键。

2024013060.en_text: The idea is based on studies of communities such as the Kung of Botswana, where each child is cared for by many adults.
2024013060.cn_text: 这一观点基于对博茨瓦纳昆族等社群的研究，在这些社群中，每个孩子都由众多成年人共同照料。

2024013061.en_text: Kung children as young as four will help to look after younger ones and “baby-wearing”, in which infants are carried in slings, is considered the norm.
2024013061.cn_text: 昆族的孩子四岁时就会帮助照顾更小的孩子，而用吊带背负婴儿的「婴儿背带」做法被视为常态。

2024013062.en_text: According to Dr Nikhil Chaudhary, an evolutionary anthropologist at Cambridge University, these practices, known as alloparenting, could lead to less anxiety for children and parents.
2024013062.cn_text: 剑桥大学进化人类学家尼基尔·乔杜里博士认为，这些被称为「协同育儿」的做法可能会减轻儿童和父母的焦虑。

2024013063.en_text: Dr Annie Swanepoel, a child psychiatrist, believes that there are ways to incorporate them into western life.
2024013063.cn_text: 儿童精神病学家安妮·斯瓦内普尔博士认为，有办法将这些做法融入西方生活。

2024013064.en_text: In Germany, one scheme has paired an old people’s home with a nursery.
2024013064.cn_text: 在德国,一项计划将一家养老院与一家托儿所配对。

2024013065.en_text: The residents help to look after the children, an arrangement akin to alloparenting.
2024013065.cn_text: 养老院的居民帮助照顾孩子,这种安排类似于协同育儿。

2024013066.en_text: Another measure could be encouraging friendships between children in different school years, to mirror the unsupervised mixed-age playgroups in hunter-gatherer communities.
2024013066.cn_text: 另一项措施可能是鼓励不同年级儿童之间建立友谊,以模仿狩猎采集社群中无人监管的混龄游戏群体。

2024013067.en_text: In a paper published in the Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry, researchers said that the western nuclear family was a recent invention which broke with evolutionary history.
2024013067.cn_text: 在《儿童心理学与精神病学杂志》上发表的一篇论文中,研究人员指出,西方核心家庭是近期出现的产物,背离了进化历史。

2024013068.en_text: This abrupt shift to an “intensive mothering narrative”, which suggests that mothers should manage childcare alone, was likely to have been harmful.
2024013068.cn_text: 这种向「密集母职叙事」的突然转变——即认为母亲应独自承担育儿责任——很可能是有害的。

2024013069.en_text: “Such narratives can lead to maternal exhaustion and have dangerous consequences,” they wrote.
2024013069.cn_text: 他们写道:「这种叙事可能导致母亲精疲力竭,并产生危险后果。」

2024013070.en_text: By contrast, in hunter-gatherer societies adults other than the parents can provide almost half of a child’s care.
2024013070.cn_text: 相比之下,在狩猎采集社会中,父母以外的成年人可以提供近一半的儿童照料。

2024013071.en_text: One previous study looked at the Efé people of the Democratic Republic of Congo.
2024013071.cn_text: 此前一项研究考察了刚果民主共和国的埃费人。

2024013072.en_text: It found that infants had an average of 14 alloparents a day by the time they were 18 weeks old, and were passed between caregivers eight times an hour.
2024013072.cn_text: 研究发现,婴儿到18周大时,平均每天有14名辅助照料者,并且每小时在照料者之间传递8次。

2024013073.en_text: Chaudhary said that parents now have less childcare support from family and social networks than during most of humans’ evolutionary history, but introducing additional caregivers could reduce stress and maternal depression, which could have a “knock-on” benefit to a child’s wellbeing.
2024013073.cn_text: 乔杜里表示,与人类进化史的大部分时期相比,如今父母从家庭和社会网络获得的育儿支持更少,但引入更多照料者可以减轻压力和产后抑郁,这可能对儿童的幸福感产生「连锁」效应。

2024013074.en_text: An infant born to a hunter-gatherer society could have more than ten caregivers — this contrasts starkly to nursery settings in the UK where regulations call for a ratio of one carer to four children aged two to three.
2024013074.cn_text: 出生在狩猎采集社会的婴儿可能有十多名照料者——这与英国托儿所的规定形成鲜明对比,后者要求两到三岁儿童每四人配一名照料者。

2024013075.en_text: While hunter-gatherer children learnt from observation and imitation in mixed-age playgroups, researchers said that western “instructive teaching”, where pupils are asked to sit still, may contribute to conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.
2024013075.cn_text: 狩猎采集社会的儿童在混龄游戏群体中通过观察和模仿学习,而研究人员指出,西方的「指导性教学」——要求学生静坐——可能导致注意力缺陷多动障碍等问题。

2024013076.en_text: Chaudhary said that Britain should explore the possibility that older siblings helping their parents “might also enhance their own social development.”
2024013076.cn_text: 乔杜里表示,英国应探索让年长子女帮助父母的可能性,这「也可能促进他们自身的社会性发展」。

2024013085.cn_text: 西方文化中的传统育儿方式

2024013086.en_text: the differences between western and African ways of living.
2024013086.cn_text: 西方与非洲生活方式之间的差异

2024013087.cn_text: 根据第4段,「密集母职叙事」____

2024013090.cn_text: 导致了以子女为中心的家庭

2024013091.en_text: departs from the course of evolution.

2024013092.en_text: According to Paragraph 6, what can we learn about the nurseries in the UK?
2024013092.cn_text: 根据第6段,关于英国的托儿所我们可以了解到什么?

2024013093.en_text: They tend to fall short of official requirements.
2024013093.cn_text: 它们往往达不到官方要求

2024013094.cn_text: 它们难以找到足够的照料者

2024013095.cn_text: 它们应该改善照料者与儿童的比例

2024013096.cn_text: 它们应该努力预防父母抑郁

2024013098.en_text: Instructive Teaching: A Dilemma for Anxious Parents
2024013098.cn_text: 指导性教学:焦虑父母的困境

2024013099.cn_text: 想要更幸福的家庭,向狩猎采集者学习

2024013100.cn_text: 混龄游戏群体:孤独儿童的更佳选择

2024013101.en_text: Tracing the History of Parenting: from Africa to Europe
2024013101.cn_text: 追溯育儿历史:从非洲到欧洲

2024013102.en_text: A Polish digital artist who uses classical painting styles to create dreamy fantasy landscapes, Greg Rutkowski has made illustrations for games such as Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering.
2024013102.cn_text: 波兰数字艺术家格雷格·鲁特科夫斯基运用古典绘画风格创作梦幻般的奇幻景观，曾为《龙与地下城》和《万智牌》等游戏绘制插图。

2024013103.en_text: And he’s become a sudden hit in the new world of text-to-image AI generation.
2024013103.cn_text: 他在文本生成图像的人工智能新领域中迅速走红。

2024013104.en_text: His distinctive style is now one of the most commonly used prompts in the new opensource AI art generator Stable Diffusion.
2024013104.cn_text: 他独特的风格现已成为新开源人工智能艺术生成器Stable Diffusion中最常用的提示词之一。

2024013105.en_text: The tool, along with other popular imagegeneration AI models, allows anyone to create impressive images based on text prompts.
2024013105.cn_text: 该工具与其他流行的图像生成人工智能模型一样，允许任何人根据文本提示创建令人印象深刻的图像。

2024013106.en_text: For example, type in “Wizard with sword and a glowing orb of magic fire fights a fierce dragon Greg Rutkowski,” and the system will produce something that looks not a million miles away from works in Rutkowski’s style.
2024013106.cn_text: 例如，输入「手持长剑和发光魔法火球的巫师与一条凶猛的龙战斗 Greg Rutkowski」，系统将生成与鲁特科夫斯基风格作品相去不远的图像。

2024013107.en_text: But these open-source programs are built by scraping images from the internet, often without permission and proper attribution to artists.
2024013107.cn_text: 但这些开源程序是通过从互联网上抓取图像构建的，往往未经许可，也未对艺术家进行适当署名。

2024013108.en_text: As a result, they are raising tricky questions about ethics and copyright.
2024013108.cn_text: 因此，它们引发了关于伦理和版权的棘手问题。

2024013109.en_text: And artists like Rutkowski have had enough.
2024013109.cn_text: 像鲁特科夫斯基这样的艺术家已经受够了。

2024013110.en_text: According to the website Lexica, which tracks over 10 million images and prompts generated by Stable Diffusion, Rutkowski’s name has been used as a prompt around 93,000 times.
2024013110.cn_text: 据追踪由Stable Diffusion生成的超过1000万张图像和提示词的网站Lexica显示，鲁特科夫斯基的名字被用作提示词约93000次。

2024013111.en_text: Rutkowski was initially surprised but thought it might be a good way to reach new audiences.
2024013111.cn_text: 鲁特科夫斯基起初感到惊讶，但认为这可能是接触新受众的好方法。

2024013112.en_text: Then he tried searching for his name to see if a piece he had worked on had been published.
2024013112.cn_text: 随后他尝试搜索自己的名字，想看看自己创作的作品是否被发表。

2024013113.en_text: The online search brought back work that had his name attached to it but wasn’t his.
2024013113.cn_text: 在线搜索结果显示，一些附有他名字的作品实际上并非他本人所作。

2024013116.en_text: I probably won’t be able to find my work out there because the internet will be flooded with AI art,” Rutkowski says.
2024013116.cn_text: 我可能无法在网上找到自己的作品了，因为互联网将被人工智能艺术淹没，」鲁特科夫斯基说。

2024013118.en_text: Other artists besides Rutkowski have been surprised by the apparent popularity of their work in text-to-image generators — and some are now fighting back.
2024013118.cn_text: 除鲁特科夫斯基外，其他艺术家也对自己作品在文本生成图像工具中的明显流行感到惊讶——一些人现在正在反击。

2024013119.en_text: Karla Ortiz, an illustrator based in San Francisco who found her work in Stable Diffusion’s data set, has been raising awareness about the issues around AI art and copyright.
2024013119.cn_text: 居住在旧金山的插画师卡拉·奥尔蒂斯发现自己的作品出现在Stable Diffusion的数据集中，并一直在提高人们对人工智能艺术和版权问题的认识。

2024013120.en_text: Artists say they risk losing income as people start using AI-generated images based on copyrighted material for commercial purposes.
2024013120.cn_text: 艺术家表示，他们面临收入损失的风险,因为人们开始将基于受版权保护材料生成的人工智能图像用于商业目的。

2024013121.en_text: But it’s also a lot more personal, Ortiz says, arguing that because art is so closely linked to a person, it could raise data protection and privacy problems.
2024013121.cn_text: 但奥尔蒂斯表示，这也更加私人化，她认为由于艺术与个人紧密相关，这可能会引发数据保护和隐私问题。

2024013122.en_text: “There is a coalition growing within artist industries to figure out how to tackle or mitigate this,” says Ortiz.
2024013122.cn_text: 「艺术家行业内正在形成一个联盟，以研究如何应对或缓解这一问题，」奥尔蒂斯说。

2024013123.en_text: The group is in its early days of mobilization, which could involve pushing for new policies or regulation.
2024013123.cn_text: 该组织正处于动员初期阶段，可能涉及推动新政策或法规的出台。

2024013124.en_text: One suggestion is that AI models could be trained on images in the public domain, and AI companies could forge partnerships with museums and artists, Ortiz says.
2024013124.cn_text: 奥尔蒂斯表示，一种建议是人工智能模型可以使用公共领域的图像进行训练，人工智能公司可以与博物馆和艺术家建立合作关系。

2024013125.en_text: What can be learned about Rutkowski from the first two paragraphs?
2024013125.cn_text: 从前两段可以了解到关于鲁特科夫斯基的哪些信息？

2024013126.en_text: He is enthusiastic about using AI models.
2024013126.cn_text: 他对使用人工智能模型充满热情。

2024013127.cn_text: 他在人工智能艺术生成器用户中很受欢迎。

2024013128.cn_text: 他赢得了其他插画师的钦佩。

2024013129.cn_text: 他专注于古典绘画的数字化。

2024013131.cn_text: 在响应提示时缺乏灵活性。

2024013133.cn_text: 未经授权使用在线图像。

2024013136.cn_text: 一种接触受众的独特方式。

2024013137.cn_text: 一种识别人工智能图像的新方法。

2024013138.cn_text: 带有他名字的人工智能生成作品。

2024013139.cn_text: 关于他版权的激烈争论。

2024013140.en_text: According to Ortiz, AI companies are advised to ____
2024013140.cn_text: 根据奥尔蒂斯的说法，建议人工智能公司____

2024013141.en_text: campaign for new policies or regulation.
2024013141.cn_text: 为新政策或法规开展宣传。

2024013142.en_text: offer their services to public institutions.

2024013143.en_text: strengthen their relationships with AI users.
2024013143.cn_text: 加强与人工智能用户的关系。

2024013144.en_text: adopt a different strategy for AI model training.
2024013144.cn_text: 为人工智能模型训练采用不同的策略。

2024013145.en_text: What is the text mainly about?

2024013146.en_text: Artists’ responses to AI art generation.
2024013146.cn_text: 艺术家对人工智能艺术生成的回应。

2024013147.en_text: AI’s expanded role in artistic creation.
2024013147.cn_text: 人工智能在艺术创作中的扩展作用。

2024013148.en_text: Privacy issues in the application of AI.
2024013148.cn_text: 人工智能应用中的隐私问题。

2024013149.cn_text: 关于人工智能发展的对立观点。

2024013150.en_text: The miracle of the Chesapeake Bay lies not in its depths, but in the complexity of its natural construction, the interaction of fresh and saline waters, and the mix of land and water.
2024013150.cn_text: 切萨皮克湾的奇迹不在于其深度，而在于其自然结构的复杂性、淡水与咸水的相互作用以及陆地与水域的交融。

2024013151.en_text: The shallows provide homes for hundreds of species while storing floodwaters, filtering pollutants from water, and protecting nearby communities from potentially destructive storm surges.
2024013151.cn_text: 浅滩为数百种生物提供栖息地，同时蓄积洪水、过滤水中污染物，并保护附近社区免受潜在破坏性风暴潮的侵袭。

2024013152.en_text: All this was put at great risk late last month, when the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling in an Idaho case that provides the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) far less authority to regulate wetlands and waterways.
2024013152.cn_text: 上月末，美国最高法院就一起爱达荷州案件作出裁决，大幅削弱了美国环保署对湿地和水道的监管权力，使所有这些都面临巨大风险。

2024013155.en_text: Specifically, a 5-4 majority decided that wetlands protected by the EPA under its Clean Water Act authority must have a “continuous surface connection” to bodies of water.
2024013155.cn_text: 具体而言，5比4的多数裁定，环保署依据《清洁水法》权限保护的湿地必须与水体存在「连续的表面连接」。

2024013156.en_text: This narrowing of the regulatory scope was a victory for builders, mining operators and other commercial interests often at odds with environmental rules.
2024013156.cn_text: 监管范围的收窄对建筑商、采矿运营商及其他常与环境法规相冲突的商业利益而言是一次胜利。

2024013157.en_text: And it carries “significant repercussions for water quality and flood control throughout the United States,” as Justice Brett Kavanaugh observed.
2024013157.cn_text: 正如布雷特·卡瓦诺大法官所指出的，此举对全美的水质和洪水治理具有「重大影响」。

2024013158.en_text: In Maryland, the good news is that there are many state laws in place that provide wetlands protections.
2024013158.cn_text: 在马里兰州，好消息是现有许多州法律提供湿地保护。

2024013159.en_text: But that’s a very shortsighted view, particularly when it comes to the Chesapeake Bay.
2024013159.cn_text: 但这是一种十分短视的看法，尤其在涉及切萨皮克湾时。

2024013160.en_text: The reality is that water, and the pollutants that so often come with it, don’t respect state boundaries.
2024013160.cn_text: 现实是，水及其常常携带的污染物并不遵守州界。

2024013161.en_text: The Chesapeake draws from a 64,000-square-mile watershed that extends into Virginia, Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia, the District of Columbia and Delaware.
2024013161.cn_text: 切萨皮克湾的水源来自一个面积达64000平方英里的流域，该流域延伸至弗吉尼亚州、宾夕法尼亚州、纽约州、西弗吉尼亚州、哥伦比亚特区和特拉华州。

2024013162.en_text: Will those jurisdictions extend the same protections now denied under Sackett v.
2024013162.cn_text: 这些司法管辖区是否会延续在Sackett诉环保署案中被否定的保护措施？

2024013164.cn_text: 或许有些会，但会全部吗？

2024013166.en_text: It is too easy, and misleading, to see such court rulings as merely standing up for the rights of land owners when the consequences can be so dire for their neighbors.
2024013166.cn_text: 将此类法院裁决仅仅视为维护土地所有者权利过于简单且具有误导性，因为其后果对邻近地区可能是极为严重的。

2024013167.en_text: And it’s a reminder that the EPA’s involvement in the Chesapeake Bay Program has long been crucial as the means to transcend the influence of deep-pocketed special interests in neighboring states.
2024013167.cn_text: 这也提醒我们，环保署参与切萨皮克湾计划长期以来一直至关重要，因为它是超越邻近各州财力雄厚的特殊利益集团影响的手段。

2024013168.en_text: Pennsylvania farmers, to use one telling example, aren’t thinking about next year’s blue crab harvest in Maryland when they decide whether to spread animal waste on their fields, yet the runoff into nearby creeks can have enormous impact downstream.
2024013168.cn_text: 以一个典型例子来说，宾夕法尼亚州的农民在决定是否将动物粪便施于田地时，并未考虑马里兰州明年的蓝蟹收成，但流入附近溪流的径流可能对下游造成巨大影响。

2024013169.en_text: And so we would call on state lawmakers from Richmond to Albany to consider reviewing their own wetlands protections and see for themselves the enormous stakes involved.
2024013169.cn_text: 因此，我们呼吁从里士满到奥尔巴尼的州立法者审查本州的湿地保护措施，并亲自了解其中涉及的巨大利害关系。

2024013170.en_text: We can offer them a visit to Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge in Dorchester County where bald eagles fly over tidal marshes so shallow you could not paddle a boat across them but teaming with aquatic life.
2024013170.cn_text: 我们可以邀请他们参观位于多切斯特县的黑水国家野生动物保护区，在那里，秃鹰飞越浅得无法行船的潮汐沼泽，但沼泽中却充满了水生生物。

2024013171.cn_text: 风景优美的驾车之旅值得一去。

2024013172.en_text: The Chesapeake Bay is described in Paragraph 1 as ____
2024013172.cn_text: 第一段将切萨皮克湾描述为____

2024013174.cn_text: 一个存在争议的保护区。

2024013175.cn_text: 一个具有商业潜力的地方。

2024013177.en_text: The U.S. Supreme Court’s ruling in the Idaho case ____
2024013177.cn_text: 美国最高法院在爱达荷州案件中的裁决____

2024013179.cn_text: 削弱了环保署的监管权力。

2024013180.en_text: will end conflicts among local residents.
2024013180.cn_text: 将终结当地居民间的冲突。

2024013181.en_text: may face opposition from mining operators.
2024013181.cn_text: 可能遭到采矿运营商的反对。

2024013182.en_text: How does the author feel about future of the Chesapeake Bay?
2024013182.cn_text: 作者对切萨皮克湾的未来持何态度？

2024013187.en_text: What can be inferred about the EPA’s involvement in the Chesapeake Bay Program?
2024013187.cn_text: 关于环保署参与切萨皮克湾计划，可以推断出什么？

2024013188.en_text: It has restored the balance among neighboring jurisdictions.
2024013188.cn_text: 它恢复了邻近司法管辖区之间的平衡。

2024013189.en_text: It has triggered a radical reform in commercial fisheries.
2024013189.cn_text: 它引发了商业渔业的根本性改革。

2024013190.en_text: It has set a fine example of respecting state authorities.
2024013190.cn_text: 它为尊重州政府权威树立了良好典范。

2024013191.en_text: It has ensured the coordination of protection efforts.
2024013191.cn_text: 它确保了保护工作的协同推进。

2024013192.en_text: The author holds that the state lawmakers should ____
2024013192.cn_text: 作者认为州立法者应该____

2024013193.en_text: be cautious about the influence of landowners.
2024013193.cn_text: 对土地所有者的影响保持警惕。

2024013194.en_text: attach due importance to wetlands protections.
2024013194.cn_text: 对湿地保护给予应有的重视。

2024013195.en_text: recognize the need to expand wildlife refuges.
2024013195.cn_text: 认识到扩大野生动物保护区的必要性。

2024013196.en_text: improve the wellbeing of endangered species.
2024013196.cn_text: 改善濒危物种的生存状况。

2024013197.en_text: Simply, there are people in Nigeria who cannot travel to the Smithsonian Institution to see that part of their history and culture represented by the Benin Bronzes.
2024013197.cn_text: 简而言之，尼日利亚有些民众无法前往史密森学会，亲睹那些代表本民族历史与文化的贝宁青铜器。

2024013198.en_text: These should be available to them as part of their cultural heritage and history and as a source of national pride.
2024013198.cn_text: 这些文物应作为其文化遗产与历史的组成部分，以及民族自豪感的源泉，向他们开放。

2024013199.en_text: There is no good reason that these artifacts should be beyond the ordinary reach of the educational objectives or inspiration of the generations to which they were left.
2024013199.cn_text: 没有充分理由使这些文物脱离其所遗留给的世代在教育目标或精神启迪方面的正常触达范围。

2024013200.en_text: They serve no purpose in a museum in the United States or elsewhere except as curious objects.
2024013200.cn_text: 它们在美国或其他地方的博物馆中除了充当猎奇展品外别无用途。

2024013201.en_text: They cannot be compared to works of art produced for sale which can be passed from hand to hand and place to place by purchase.
2024013201.cn_text: 它们不能与为销售而创作的艺术品相提并论，后者可以通过购买行为在不同所有者与不同地点之间流转。

2024013202.en_text: We know very exact reproductions of artwork can be and are regularly produced.
2024013202.cn_text: 我们知道极为精确的艺术品复制品能够并且经常被制作出来。

2024013203.en_text: Perhaps museums and governments might explore some role for the use of nearly exact reproductions as a means of resolving issues relating to returning works of art and antiquities.
2024013203.cn_text: 或许博物馆和政府可以探索利用高度精确的复制品来解决艺术品与古物归还问题的可能性。

2024013204.en_text: The context of any exhibit is more important to me than whether the object being displayed is 2000 years old or 2 months old.
2024013204.cn_text: 对我而言，任何展览的背景语境比展品本身是两千年前的还是两个月前的更加重要。

2024013205.en_text: In many cases the experts have a hard time agreeing on what is the real object and what is a forgery.
2024013205.cn_text: 很多情况下，专家们很难就何为真品、何为赝品达成共识。

2024013206.en_text: Again, the story an exhibit is trying to tell is what matters.
2024013206.cn_text: 再者，展览所试图讲述的故事才是关键所在。

2024013207.en_text: The monetary value of the objects on display is a distant second place in importance.
2024013207.cn_text: 展品的货币价值在重要性上远居其次。

2024013208.en_text: When visiting the Baltimore Museum of Art, I came across a magnificent 15th-century Chinese sculpture.
2024013208.cn_text: 参观巴尔的摩艺术博物馆时,我偶然发现了一件精美的十五世纪中国雕塑。

2024013209.en_text: It inspired me to learn more about the culture that it represented.
2024013209.cn_text: 它激发了我深入了解其所代表文化的兴趣。

2024013210.en_text: Artifacts in museums have the power to inspire, and perhaps spark that need to learn and understand the nature of their creators.
2024013210.cn_text: 博物馆中的文物具有启迪心智的力量，或许还能激发人们学习并理解其创造者本质的需求。

2024013211.en_text: Having said that, I do feel that whatever artifacts find their way to public museums should, in fact, be sanctioned as having been obtained on loan, legally purchased, or obtained by treaty.
2024013211.cn_text: 话虽如此，我确实认为，凡是进入公共博物馆的文物都应经确认系通过租借、合法购买或条约获得。

2024013212.en_text: Stealing artifacts from other peoples’ cultures is obscene; it robs not only the physical objects, but the dignity and spirit of their creators.
2024013212.cn_text: 从他人文化中窃取文物是可憎行径；它不仅剥夺了实物本身，还践踏了其创造者的尊严与精神。

2024013213.en_text: Ancient art that is displayed in foreign countries by all means should be returned to the original country.
2024013213.cn_text: 在外国展示的古代艺术品无论如何都应归还原属国。

2024013214.en_text: The foreign countries have no right to hold back returning the items.
2024013214.cn_text: 外国无权阻止归还这些物品。

2024013215.en_text: I would ask that the foreign nations and the original country discuss the terms of transfer.
2024013215.cn_text: 我希望外国与原属国就移交条款进行协商。

2024013216.en_text: Yes, there is the risk that the original country will not have as good security as do the foreign countries.
2024013216.cn_text: 诚然，原属国的安全保障可能不如外国完善。

2024013217.en_text: But look at what happened to Boston’s Gardner Museum theft in 1990, including the loss of Rembrandt, Vermeer, Manet, and other masterpieces.
2024013217.cn_text: 但看看1990年波士顿加德纳博物馆的盗窃案，包括伦勃朗、维米尔、马奈等大师杰作的失窃。

2024013218.cn_text: 没有任何地方绝对安全。

2024013219.en_text: And now Climate Change agitators are attacking publicly displayed works in European museums.
2024013219.cn_text: 而今气候变化激进分子正在袭击欧洲博物馆公开陈列的作品。

2024013220.en_text: To those of you in the comments section who are having strong feelings about artifacts being removed from cities in the US and Britain and returned to their countries of origin, I would ask you to consider: why do you think Americans have more of a right to easily access the Benin Bronzes than the people of Nigeria?
2024013220.cn_text: 对于评论区中对文物从美英城市移除并归还原属国抱有强烈情绪的诸位，我想请你们思考：为何你们认为美国人比尼日利亚人更有权便捷地接触贝宁青铜器？

2024013221.en_text: Why are people who live within a day’s drive of London entitled to go and see the Elgin Marbles whenever they want, but the people of Athens aren’t?
2024013221.cn_text: 为何居住在伦敦一日车程范围内的人可以随时观赏埃尔金大理石雕，而雅典人却不能？

2024013222.en_text: What intrinsic factors make the West a suitable home for these artifacts but preclude them from being preserved and displayed by their countries of origin?
2024013222.cn_text: 何种内在因素使西方成为这些文物的适宜归宿，却将其在原属国保存与展示的可能性排除在外？

2024013223.en_text: If your conclusion is that the West is better able to preserve these artifacts, think about why you’re assuming that to be true.
2024013223.cn_text: 若你的结论是西方更有能力保存这些文物，请思考一下为何你会如此假定。

2024013224.en_text: It is clear that the countries of origin have never been compensated for the stolen artifacts.
2024013224.cn_text: 显而易见，原属国从未因被盗文物获得补偿。

2024013225.en_text: It is a flawed line of reasoning to argue against returning artifacts to their countries of origin.
2024013225.cn_text: 反对将文物归还原属国的推理存在缺陷。

2024013226.en_text: Museum visitors can still learn as much from artifacts’ copies after the originals are returned.
2024013226.cn_text: 原件归还后，博物馆参观者仍能从文物复制品中获取同等的知识。

2024013227.en_text: Reproductions, even if perfectly made, cannot take the place of the authentic objects.
2024013227.cn_text: 复制品即使制作得再精良，也无法替代真品。

2024013228.en_text: The real value of artifacts can only be recognized in their countries of origin rather than anywhere else.
2024013228.cn_text: 文物的真正价值只有在其原属国才能得到体现，而非其他任何地方。

2024013229.en_text: Ways to get artifacts from other countries must be decent and lawful.
2024013229.cn_text: 从他国获取文物的方式必须正当且合法。

2024013230.en_text: Concern over security is no excuse for refusing to return artifacts to their countries of origin.
2024013230.cn_text: 对安全的担忧不能成为拒绝将文物归还原属国的理由。

2024013231.en_text: “Elephants never forget” — or so they say — and that piece of folklore seems to have some foundation.
2024013231.cn_text: 「大象永不忘记」——人们常这样说——而这一民间传说似乎确有几分根据。

2024013232.en_text: The African savanna elephant, also known as the African bush elephant, is distributed across 37 African countries.
2024013232.cn_text: 非洲草原象，亦称非洲灌木象,分布于37个非洲国家。

2024013233.en_text: They move between a variety of habitats, including forests, grasslands, woodlands, wetlands and agricultural land.
2024013233.cn_text: 它们在森林、草原、林地、湿地和农田等多种栖息地之间迁徙活动。

2024013234.en_text: They sometimes travel more than sixty miles to find food or water, and are very good at working out where other elephants are — even when they are out of sight.
2024013234.cn_text: 它们有时会跋涉六十多英里寻找食物或水源，并且极为擅长判定其他大象的位置——即便在视野之外。

2024013235.en_text: Using tracking devices, researchers have shown that they have “remarkable spatial acuity.” When finding their way to waterholes, they headed off in exactly the right direction, on one occasion from a distance of roughly thirty miles.
2024013235.cn_text: 借助追踪设备，研究人员发现它们具有「非凡的空间敏锐性」。在前往水坑时，它们朝着完全正确的方向出发，有一次甚至从约三十英里外启程。

2024013236.en_text: What is more, they almost always seem to choose the nearest waterhole.
2024013236.cn_text: 而且，它们几乎总是选择最近的水坑。

2024013237.en_text: The researchers are convinced that the elephants always know precisely where they are in relation to all the resources they need, and can therefore take shortcuts, as well as following familiar routes.
2024013237.cn_text: 研究人员确信，大象始终精确掌握自身与所需各类资源的相对位置，因此既能抄近路，也能沿熟悉的路线行进。

2024013238.en_text: Although the cues used by African elephants for long-distance navigation are not yet understood, smell may well play a part.
2024013238.cn_text: 虽然非洲象用于长距离导航的线索尚不明确，但嗅觉很可能在其中发挥作用。

2024013239.en_text: Elephants are very choosy eaters, but until recently little was known about how they selected their food.
2024013239.cn_text: 大象对食物极为挑剔，但直到最近，人们对它们如何选择食物仍知之甚少。

2024013240.en_text: One possibility was that they merely used their eyes and tried out the plants they found, but that would probably result in a lot of wasted time and energy, not least because their eyesight is actually not very good.
2024013240.cn_text: 一种可能是它们仅凭视觉观察并尝试所发现的植物，但这很可能导致大量时间和精力的浪费，尤其是因为它们的视力其实并不佳。

2024013241.en_text: The volatile chemicals produced by plants can be carried a long way, and they are very characteristic: Each plant or tree has its own particular odor signature.
2024013241.cn_text: 植物产生的挥发性化学物质可以远距离传播，且特征十分鲜明：每种植物或树木都有其独特的气味标识。

2024013242.en_text: What is more, they can be detected even when they are not actually visible.
2024013242.cn_text: 而且，即使它们实际上不可见，这些气味也能被探测到。

2024013243.en_text: New research suggests that smell is a crucial factor in guiding elephants — and probably other herbivores — to the best food resources.
2024013243.cn_text: 新研究表明，嗅觉是引导大象——也可能包括其他食草动物——找到最佳食物资源的关键因素。

2024013244.en_text: The researchers first established what kinds of plant the elephants preferred either to eat or avoid when foraging freely.
2024013244.cn_text: 研究人员首先确定了大象在自由觅食时偏好取食或回避的植物种类。

2024013245.en_text: They then set up a “food station” experiment, in which they gave the elephants a series of choices based only on smell.
2024013245.cn_text: 随后他们设置了「食物站」实验，在实验中仅依据气味向大象提供一系列选择。

2024013246.en_text: The experiment showed that elephants may well use smell to identify patches of trees that are good to eat, and secondly to assess the quality of the trees within each patch.
2024013246.cn_text: 实验表明，大象很可能利用嗅觉识别适宜取食的树木片区，其次评估各片区内树木的质量。

2024013247.en_text: Free-ranging elephants presumably also use this information to locate their preferred food.
2024013247.cn_text: 自由活动的大象想必也利用这些信息来定位其偏好的食物。

2024013248.en_text: Their well-developed hippocampal structures may enable elephants, like rats and people, to construct cognitive maps.
2024013248.cn_text: 它们发育良好的海马结构可能使大象像老鼠和人类一样，能够构建认知地图。

2025013001.en_text: Located in the southern Peloponnesian peninsula, Pavlopetri (the modern name of the site) emerged as a Neolithic settlement around 3500 B.C.
2025013001.cn_text: 帕夫洛佩特里（该遗址的现代名称）位于伯罗奔尼撒半岛南部，约在公元前3500年作为新石器时代聚落出现。

2025013002.en_text: This area of the Aegean Sea is prone to earthquakes and tsunamis, which caused the city to gradually sink.
2025013002.cn_text: 爱琴海的这一区域易发地震和海啸，导致该城市逐渐下沉。

2025013003.en_text: The slow sea level rise in the Mediterranean submerged the city more than 3,000 years ago.
2025013003.cn_text: 地中海海平面的缓慢上升使这座城市在三千多年前被淹没。

2025013004.en_text: For millennia, the city’s remains lay unseen below some 13 feet of water.
2025013004.cn_text: 数千年来，这座城市的遗迹一直隐没在约13英尺深的水下。

2025013005.en_text: They were covered by a thick layer of sand off the island of Laconia.
2025013005.cn_text: 它们被拉科尼亚岛外一层厚厚的沙层覆盖。

2025013006.en_text: In recent decades, shifting currents and climate change have eroded a natural barrier that protected Pavlopetri.
2025013006.cn_text: 近几十年来，洋流变化和气候变化侵蚀了保护帕夫洛佩特里的天然屏障。

2025013007.en_text: In 1967, a scientific survey of the Peloponnesian coast was gathering data to analyze changes in sea levels when British oceanographer Nicholas Flemming first spotted the sunken structures.
2025013007.cn_text: 1967年，一项对伯罗奔尼撒海岸的科学调查正在收集数据以分析海平面变化，英国海洋学家尼古拉斯·弗莱明首次发现了这些沉没的建筑结构。

2025013008.en_text: A year later, he returned with a few students to examine the location and map the site.
2025013008.cn_text: 一年后，他带着几名学生返回，对该地点进行考察并绘制遗址地图。

2025013009.en_text: The team identified some 15 buildings, courtyards, a network of streets, and two chamber tombs.
2025013009.cn_text: 该团队识别出约15座建筑、庭院、一个街道网络以及两座墓室。

2025013010.en_text: Despite the exciting initial finds, the site would lie undisturbed for decades before archaeologists would return.
2025013010.cn_text: 尽管初步发现令人振奋，该遗址在几十年间未受扰动，直到考古学家再次返回。

2025013011.en_text: In 2009 archaeologists Chrysanthi Gallon and Jon Henderson resumed excavation of Pavlopetri in cooperation with the Greek Ministry of Culture.
2025013011.cn_text: 2009年，考古学家克丽桑西·加隆和乔恩·亨德森与希腊文化部合作，重启了对帕夫洛佩特里的发掘工作。

2025013012.en_text: Since the 1960s, underwater archaeology techniques and tools had made huge advances.
2025013012.cn_text: 自20世纪60年代以来，水下考古技术和工具已取得巨大进步。

2025013013.en_text: The team employed robotics, sonar mapping, and state-of-the-art graphics to survey the site.
2025013013.cn_text: 该团队运用机器人技术、声纳测绘和最先进的图形技术对遗址进行勘测。

2025013014.en_text: From 2009 to 2013 they were able to bring the underwater town to light.
2025013014.cn_text: 从2009年到2013年，他们成功使这座水下城镇重见天日。

2025013015.en_text: Covering about two and a half acres, Pavlopetri’s three main roads connected some 50 rectangular buildings, all of which had open courtyards.
2025013015.cn_text: 帕夫洛佩特里占地约两英亩半，三条主干道连接着约50座矩形建筑，所有建筑均设有开放式庭院。

2025013016.en_text: Excavations revealed a large number of Minoan-style loom weights, suggesting Pavlopetri was a thriving trade center with a robust textile industry.
2025013016.cn_text: 发掘出大量米诺斯风格的织机配重，表明帕夫洛佩特里是一个繁荣的贸易中心，拥有强大的纺织产业。

2025013017.en_text: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after groundbreaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children’s literacy and emotional development.
2025013017.cn_text: 这位来自埃文河畔斯特拉特福的文法学校学生取得了学术上的重大突破，开创性研究表明莎士比亚确实有益于儿童的读写能力和情感发展。

2025013018.en_text: But only if you act him out.
2025013018.cn_text: 但前提是你要将其表演出来。

2025013019.en_text: A study found that a “rehearsal room” approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened children’s vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy.
2025013019.cn_text: 一项研究发现，采用「排练室」方法教授莎士比亚能够拓宽儿童的词汇量，增强其写作的复杂性，并提升他们的情感素养。

2025013020.en_text: “The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves,” Jacqui O’Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said.
2025013020.cn_text: 委托该研究的皇家莎士比亚剧团的杰奎·奥汉隆表示：「研究表明，演员的工作方式对儿童使用语言的方式以及他们对自我的认知产生重大影响。」

2025013021.en_text: The randomised control trial involved hundreds of year 5 pupils — aged nine and ten — at 45 state primary schools that had not been “previously exposed to RSC pedagogy.” They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand following the shipwreck in The Tempest.
2025013021.cn_text: 这项随机对照试验涉及45所公立小学的数百名五年级学生——年龄为九至十岁——这些学校此前未曾「接触过皇家莎士比亚剧团的教学法」。学生被分为实验组和对照组,并被要求完成写作任务,例如以《暴风雨》中费迪南德的身份,在海难后写一封瓶中信。

2025013022.en_text: The target group were given a 30-minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage.
2025013022.cn_text: 实验组学生被安排了一项30分钟的戏剧活动来配合该段落的学习。

2025013023.en_text: The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words “classed as more sophisticated or rarer”, and wrote at greater length.
2025013023.cn_text: 经同行评审的结果显示,实验组学生使用了更广泛的词汇,运用了「被归类为更复杂或更罕见」的词语,且写作篇幅更长。

2025013024.en_text: They also “appear to be more comfortable writing in role...while [control] pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked, [target] children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character’s emotion”.
2025013024.cn_text: 他们还「似乎更能适应角色写作……而对照组学生想象的是自己在海难中的反应,实验组学生则设身处地体会文学角色,并表达该角色的情感」。

2025013025.en_text: The Time to Act study, which is published by the RSC this week, also found that while control pupils relied on “desert island clichés” such as palm trees, target pupils were “more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions”.
2025013025.cn_text: 皇家莎士比亚剧团本周发布的《行动的时机》研究还发现,对照组学生依赖于诸如椰子树等「荒岛陈词滥调」,而实验组学生则「更具扩展性,呈现了更广阔的天空、海洋和大气状况的画面」。

2025013026.en_text: O’Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the “emotional literacy that was evident in the [target] children’s writing” and that they were “more resilient in their writing, more hopeful”.
2025013026.cn_text: 奥汉隆表示,她最为惊讶的是实验组儿童写作中体现出的「情感素养」,以及他们「在写作中更具韧性,更加乐观」。

2025013027.en_text: She added “The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through.
2025013027.cn_text: 她补充道:「情感理解非常明显,这可能与排练室过程有关,在那里你习惯于尝试通过想象来体会。」

2025013028.en_text: They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes.” The study showed the importance of embedding arts in education, she said.
2025013028.cn_text: 他们能够自如地描述不同的情感状态,而戏剧活动的一部分就是让自己设身处地体会不同的角色。她表示,该研究显示了将艺术融入教育的重要性。

2025013029.en_text: But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist?
2025013029.cn_text: 但这一结果能否在任何其他剧作家身上得以复制?

2025013030.en_text: O’Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare’s use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a “massive expansion of language into children’s lives”, which was combined with children “using their whole bodies to bring words to life”.
2025013030.cn_text: 奥汉隆表示还需要更多研究,但她指出,莎士比亚使用了约2万个词汇,而日常语言仅约2000个词汇,这为儿童的生活带来了「语言的大幅扩展」,并且结合了儿童「用整个身体使语言变得生动」的方式。

2025013056.en_text: I was shocked to learn recently that some scientists want to scale back their research in an effort to decrease carbon emissions.
2025013056.cn_text: 我最近得知一些科学家想要缩减其研究规模以减少碳排放，对此我感到震惊。

2025013057.en_text: The crisis is here, they said, and we need to cut back on our energy-intensive modelling.
2025013057.cn_text: 他们说，危机已经到来,我们需要削减高耗能的建模工作。

2025013058.en_text: At the very least, we need to make our energy use far more sustainable.
2025013058.cn_text: 至少，我们需要使能源使用更具可持续性。

2025013059.en_text: It is unarguable that our laboratories, scientific instruments, rockets and satellites — the tools we scientists need to measure the planet’s pulse — demand significant amounts of energy both in their construction and operation.
2025013059.cn_text: 毋庸置疑的是，我们的实验室、科学仪器、火箭和卫星——我们科学家用来测量地球脉搏的工具——在建造和运行过程中都需要大量能源。

2025013060.en_text: And it is equally true that science’s unrelenting appetite for information has caused a mushrooming of energy-intensive data centres around the world.
2025013060.cn_text: 同样不可否认的是，科学对信息永不满足的渴求导致全球能源密集型数据中心激增。

2025013061.en_text: According to the International Energy Agency, these buildings now consume about 1 percent of the world’s electricity.
2025013061.cn_text: 据国际能源署统计，这些建筑目前消耗了全球约1%的电力。

2025013062.en_text: However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world.
2025013062.cn_text: 然而，这是我们理解世界必须付出的代价。

2025013063.en_text: How can we inform decision makers about the best ways to bring down carbon emissions if we can’t track the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, where it’s coming from and who’s producing it?
2025013063.cn_text: 如果我们无法追踪大气中二氧化碳的含量、其来源及其制造者，又如何能够向决策者提供降低碳排放的最佳方案呢？

2025013064.en_text: The carbon emissions from technological research are well spent: ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet.
2025013064.cn_text: 技术研究产生的碳排放是值得的：这些研究最终将保障我们星球的未来。

2025013065.en_text: It can be hard for scientists to make the case because our work is complex, often takes place behind closed doors and does not always lend itself to easy interpretation or explanation.
2025013065.cn_text: 科学家们可能很难证明这一点，因为我们的工作复杂，常在闭门环境中进行，且并非总是易于理解或解释。

2025013066.en_text: But demonstrating the efficacy of science will be crucial if we are to solve humanity’s greatest challenges.
2025013066.cn_text: 但若要解决人类面临的最大挑战，证明科学的有效性将至关重要。

2025013067.en_text: It is all too easy to feel paralysed in the face of daunting problems such as climate change and to do nothing.
2025013067.cn_text: 面对气候变化等艰巨问题时，很容易感到无力而无所作为。

2025013068.en_text: But then I think of a friend’s daughter who turned her fears into action: she became a wind energy engineer and now thrives on delivering renewable energy, limiting emissions.
2025013068.cn_text: 但随后我想到一位朋友的女儿，她将恐惧转化为行动：她成为了风能工程师，现在致力于提供可再生能源、限制排放，并在此领域蓬勃发展。

2025013069.en_text: Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize, which is now entering its 20th year as a celebration of human ingenuity.
2025013069.cn_text: 认识到科学与工程能够带来的希望，正是创立千年技术奖的推动力，该奖项如今已进入第20个年头，旨在颂扬人类的创造力。

2025013070.en_text: One of the past winners, Professor Martin Green from the University of New South Wales, Australia, is the inventor of the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell technology which is now found in most of the world’s solar panels.
2025013070.cn_text: 过去的一位获奖者是澳大利亚新南威尔士大学的马丁·格林教授，他是钝化发射极和背面电池技术的发明者，该技术如今应用于全球大部分太阳能电池板。

2025013071.en_text: Thanks to his invention, we have a real chance to decrease the world’s carbon emissions.
2025013071.cn_text: 借助他的发明，我们有了切实的机会来减少全球碳排放。

2025013072.en_text: Every day, scientists, technologists and engineers are discovering new ways to exploit renewable energy sources and develop techniques not just to use power more intelligently but to power our intelligence.
2025013072.cn_text: 每天，科学家、技术专家和工程师都在发现利用可再生能源的新途径，并开发各种技术，不仅能更智能地使用电力，还能为我们的智能提供动力。

2025013073.en_text: A great example of this is Europe’s largest supercomputer, LUMI in Finland, which is astonishingly carbon-negative.
2025013073.cn_text: 一个极佳的例子是欧洲最大的超级计算机——位于芬兰的LUMI，其碳排放量令人惊讶地实现了负值。

2025013074.en_text: Established in an old paper mill, it is powered by a nearby river and its remote heat warms the people who live in the surrounding town of Kajaani.
2025013074.cn_text: 它建于一座旧造纸厂内，由附近河流供电，其余热为周边小镇卡亚尼的居民供暖。

2025013075.en_text: If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.
2025013075.cn_text: 若要实现全球净零排放目标，我们必须认真思考如何实现可持续计算并打造更多像LUMI这样的项目。

2025013101.en_text: Ever since taking on Netflix Inc. at its own game, old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming, with the likes of Disney+, Peacock and Paramount+ losing billions of dollars each year, sparking concerns that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was.
2025013101.cn_text: 自从在流媒体领域挑战 Netflix 公司以来,传统好莱坞一直难以实现盈利,Disney+、Peacock 和 Paramount+ 等平台每年亏损数十亿美元,引发了人们对这些服务能否像有线电视曾经那样盈利的担忧。

2025013103.en_text: But the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions.
2025013103.cn_text: 但流媒体时代却让一些意想不到的赢家获益:盗版者使用软件在几秒钟内从合法在线视频平台上翻录电影或电视节目,并将这些内容托管在自己的非法服务上,这些服务每年通过广告和订阅赚取约 20 亿美元。

2025013104.en_text: With no video production costs, illegal streaming sites have achieved profit margins approaching 90%, according to the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing Hollywood studios that’s working to crack down on the thousands of illegal platforms that have cropped up in recent years.
2025013104.cn_text: 据代表好莱坞制片厂并致力于打击近年来涌现的数千个非法平台的行业组织电影协会称,由于没有视频制作成本,非法流媒体网站的利润率接近 90%。

2025013105.en_text: Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads.
2025013105.cn_text: 最初,像 Netflix 这样的合法在线业务的兴起实际上帮助遏制了主要基于文件上传的数字盗版行为。

2025013106.en_text: But now piracy involving illegal streaming services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs, estimates the US Chamber of Commerce’s Global Innovation Policy Center.
2025013106.cn_text: 但现在,据美国商会全球创新政策中心估算,涉及非法流媒体服务以及文件共享的盗版行为每年给美国经济造成约 300 亿美元的收入损失和大约 25 万个就业岗位的流失。

2025013107.en_text: The global impact is about $71 billion annually.
2025013107.cn_text: 全球影响每年约为 710 亿美元。

2025013108.en_text: “The people who are stealing our movies and our television shows and operating piracy sites are not mom and pop operations,” says Charlie Rivkin, chief executive officer of the MPA.
2025013108.cn_text: 电影协会首席执行官查理·里夫金表示:「那些盗窃我们的电影和电视节目并运营盗版网站的人并非夫妻店式的小作坊,这是有组织的犯罪。」

2025013109.en_text: “This is organized crime.” Rivkin joined the MPA in 2017 after the organization failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy.
2025013109.cn_text: 里夫金于 2017 年加入电影协会,此前该组织在五年前未能在好莱坞和硅谷之间达成共识,以推动国会通过旨在打击网络盗版的立法。

2025013110.en_text: In 2017 the association formed the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), an enforcement task force of about 100 detectives circling the globe to help local authorities arrest streaming pirates.
2025013110.cn_text: 2017 年,该协会成立了创意与娱乐联盟,这是一个由约 100 名侦探组成的执法工作组,在全球范围内协助地方当局逮捕流媒体盗版者。

2025013111.en_text: ACE says it’s helped shrink the number of illegal streaming services in North America to 126, from more than 1,400 in 2018, aided in part by the MPA’s support for a 2020 federal law that made large-scale streaming of copyright material a serious crime.
2025013111.cn_text: 创意与娱乐联盟表示,它已帮助将北美非法流媒体服务的数量从 2018 年的 1400 多个减少到 126 个,这部分得益于电影协会支持的一项 2020 年联邦法律,该法律将大规模传播版权材料定为严重犯罪。

2025013112.en_text: Consulting firm Parks Associates predicts that legitimate US streaming services’ cumulative loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years.
2025013112.cn_text: 咨询公司 Parks Associates 预测,自 2022 年以来,美国合法流媒体服务因盗版造成的累计损失将在未来两年内达到 1130 亿美元。

2025013113.en_text: “While there is some optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline,” says analyst Steve Hawley.
2025013113.cn_text: 分析师史蒂夫·霍利表示:「尽管有些人乐观地认为,新兴的应对措施和最佳实践可能会使盗版在 2027 年前趋于平稳,但利益相关者之间对于盗版何时开始减少并未达成共识。」

2025013139.en_text: Visit any antiques store and you’ll encounter artifacts from the past: photographs, letters, a brochure detailing the Sinclair dinosaur exhibit from the 1964-1965 World’s Fair, the ephemera of history.
2025013139.cn_text: 走进任何一家古董店，你都会看到来自过去的文物：照片、信件、一本详细介绍1964-1965年世界博览会辛克莱恐龙展的宣传册，这些都是历史的短暂遗存。

2025013140.en_text: Yet these objects aren’t truly ephemeral, because they’re still here, decades, even centuries later.
2025013140.cn_text: 然而，这些物品并非真正短暂，因为它们仍然存在，历经数十年甚至数百年之后。

2025013143.en_text: Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation?
2025013143.cn_text: 你是否思考过无形格式、数字信息的生命周期？要知道这些信息的生产者很少为其长期保存做准备。

2025013144.en_text: For millennia, we’ve known what we’ve known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original creators’ neglect.
2025013144.cn_text: 数千年来，我们所知的历史源于幸存的文物，而这些文物往往是在其最初创造者的疏忽下保存下来的。

2025013145.en_text: The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information.
2025013145.cn_text: 物品本身就是传递信息的媒介。

2025013146.en_text: At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on.
2025013146.cn_text: 在创造之初，人们没有做任何有意保存的尝试，但模拟材料有可能幸存下来，并成为传记作者、历史学家和小说家所依赖的历史记录。

2025013147.en_text: Libraries and archives have traditionally shouldered the responsibility of organization, preservation, and access to information.
2025013147.cn_text: 图书馆和档案馆历来承担着组织、保存和提供信息获取的责任。

2025013148.en_text: Thus, librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings.
2025013148.cn_text: 因此，图书管理员将有形资料数字化，使世界各地的研究人员能够快速检索和访问这些馆藏。

2025013149.en_text: The result is an embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.
2025013149.cn_text: 结果是历史资源极为丰富，这也带来了大海捞针般的难题。

2025013150.en_text: Librarians’ selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cellphone and saying, “it’s all in here” as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today.
2025013150.cn_text: 当用户举起手机并说「都在这里面」，以此作为图书馆对当今研究人员的重要性降低的证据时，图书管理员的无私奉献可能会对我们不利。

2025013151.en_text: Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more importantly, how is it maintained?
2025013151.cn_text: 然而，这种普遍获取是如何实现的？更重要的是，它是如何维持的？

2025013152.cn_text: 谁来管理保存哪些内容？

2025013153.en_text: When it comes to born-digital information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one.
2025013153.cn_text: 对于数字原生信息而言，可怕的答案可能是：如果不是图书管理员和档案管理员，那就无人负责。

2025013154.en_text: Digital information requires a great deal more care than analog.
2025013154.cn_text: 数字信息比模拟信息需要多得多的维护。

2025013155.en_text: Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that’s saved, not the information itself.
2025013155.cn_text: 即使数字对象被保存下来，可能也只是载体得以保存，而非信息本身。

2025013156.en_text: As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless.
2025013156.cn_text: 随着技术进步，格式变得过时，这些对象便失去了用处。

2025013157.en_text: Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this?
2025013157.cn_text: 你是否曾无助地盯着一张ZIP磁盘，心想：我该如何从中提取文件？

2025013158.en_text: Without constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replace analog.
2025013158.cn_text: 如果不持续迁移数字资产，一个关于可预见未来的噩梦会让历史学家夜不能寐：当数字替代模拟时，历史记录会戛然而止。

2025013159.en_text: As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians, and I’d be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists.
2025013159.cn_text: 作为一名日常工作涉及特藏和数字资产的图书管理员，我与历史学家有着同样的担忧，如果我说目前已有全面的保存方案，那就是在撒谎。

2025013160.en_text: Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers current and future.
2025013160.cn_text: 然而，研究人员可以稍感宽慰的是，有众多图书管理员致力于为当前和未来的研究人员发现、组织和保存数字信息。

2025013161.en_text: Librarians are uniquely positioned to understand how end users seek and use information.
2025013161.cn_text: 图书管理员在理解最终用户如何查找和使用信息方面具有独特优势。

2025013162.en_text: Thus we play an integral role in identifying, preserving, and providing accessibility to digital artifacts so that, while future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to ply their trade, they won’t find it an impossible one.
2025013162.cn_text: 因此，我们在识别、保存和提供数字文物的可访问性方面发挥着不可或缺的作用，这样一来，尽管未来的研究人员可能会发现数字领域是个充满挑战的工作场所,但不会觉得完全无从下手。

2025013183.en_text: Which of the following statements best summarizes the text?

2025013184.en_text: Hard work should be done to preserve artifacts.

2025013186.en_text: Accessing databases is essential to researchers.
