2025013187.en_text: Keeping digital historical records is a challenge.
2025013187.cn_text: 保存数字历史记录是一项挑战。

2025013188.en_text: Peters likes to photograph butterflies in a landscape, celebrating the beauty of their surroundings as well as the insects themselves.
2025013188.cn_text: 彼得斯喜欢在风景中拍摄蝴蝶，既颂扬昆虫本身，也礼赞其周围环境之美。

2025013189.en_text: His pictures of a Glanville fritillary rising from the sea-pinks beside the chalk cliffs of Compton Bay on the Isle of Wight are particularly glorious.
2025013189.cn_text: 他拍摄的格兰维尔豹蛱蝶从怀特岛康普顿湾白垩悬崖旁的海石竹中振翅而起的照片尤为壮美。

2025013190.en_text: These take-off shots are even more challenging because they require a wide-angle lens, which means he must be less than 2cm from the butterfly.
2025013190.cn_text: 这些起飞镜头更具挑战性，因为需要使用广角镜头，这意味着他与蝴蝶的距离必须不到2厘米。

2025013191.en_text: It’s incredibly difficult to get that close to a skittish sun-warmed insect.
2025013191.cn_text: 要如此接近一只受阳光温暖而变得敏感易惊的昆虫，难度极大。

2025013192.en_text: Unlike some photographers, who “cheat” by keeping insects in a fridge to slow them down, Peters refuses to tamper with wild butterflies.
2025013192.cn_text: 不同于某些摄影师将昆虫置于冰箱中减缓其活动的「作弊」做法，彼得斯拒绝干扰野生蝴蝶。

2025013193.en_text: Peters’ signature shot is a butterfly “take-off”, showing the multiple wing-beats of one butterfly in one frame as it lifts off from a flower.
2025013193.cn_text: 彼得斯的标志性作品是蝴蝶「起飞」照片，在单帧画面中展现一只蝴蝶从花朵上起飞时的多次振翅动作。

2025013194.cn_text: 他是如何捕捉到这一画面的？

2025013196.en_text: A typical digital SLR camera shoots 20 frames a second.
2025013196.cn_text: 一台典型的数码单反相机每秒拍摄20帧。

2025013197.en_text: He uses a high-speed OM System which shoots 120 frames a second.
2025013197.cn_text: 他使用的高速OM系统相机每秒可拍摄120帧。

2025013198.en_text: Britain has relatively few butterfly species compared with mainland Europe and 80% are in decline, mostly because intensive chemical farming has reduced many species to tiny fragments of habitat and small nature reserves.
2025013198.cn_text: 与欧洲大陆相比，英国的蝴蝶物种相对较少，其中80%的物种数量正在减少，主要原因是集约化化学农业将许多物种的栖息地缩减为零散碎片和小型自然保护区。

2025013199.en_text: Global heating is benefiting some species but others are too isolated to find suitable new habitat, and gardening habits — paving over gardens and using pesticides — aren’t helping either.
2025013199.cn_text: 全球变暖使某些物种受益，但其他物种因过于孤立而无法找到合适的新栖息地，而园艺习惯——如用硬质铺装覆盖花园和使用杀虫剂——同样无益。

2025013200.en_text: Butterflies may not pollinate as many plants as wild bees and hoverflies, but because British butterflies are the best-studied group of insects in the world, they are an extremely useful indicator of the wider declines in flying insects.
2025013200.cn_text: 蝴蝶的授粉能力或许不及野生蜜蜂和食蚜蝇，但由于英国蝴蝶是世界上研究最为充分的昆虫类群，它们成为飞行昆虫广泛衰退的极有价值的指示物种。

2025013201.en_text: Five years ago, at summer’s end, Andrew Fusek Peters was diagnosed with bowel cancer.
2025013201.cn_text: 五年前夏末，安德鲁·福塞克·彼得斯被诊断患有肠癌。

2025013202.en_text: “I was waiting for surgery, feeling really ill, sitting in my garden.
2025013202.cn_text: 「我在等待手术，感觉非常不适，坐在自家花园里。

2025013203.en_text: It was amazing weather and there were painted lady butterflies everywhere,” he says.
2025013203.cn_text: 天气极好，到处都是赤蛱蝶，」他说。

2025013204.en_text: “They were a symbol of fragile life, of hope and defiance, and something appealed to my soul.”
2025013204.cn_text: 「它们是脆弱生命的象征，是希望与抗争的象征，某种东西触动了我的灵魂。」

2025013205.en_text: That makes it sound easy, and artificial, but Peters insists it is still a massive challenge.
2025013205.cn_text: 这使得拍摄听起来既简单又做作，但彼得斯坚称这仍是一项巨大的挑战。

2025013206.en_text: He typically takes between 10,000 and 20,000 shots to get one butterfly take-off sequence in focus.
2025013206.cn_text: 他通常需要拍摄一万到两万张照片，才能获得一组对焦清晰的蝴蝶起飞序列。

2025013207.en_text: At such high shutter speeds, the depth of field is tiny, and as butterflies do not fly in a straight line they swiftly flutter out of focus.
2025013207.cn_text: 在如此高的快门速度下，景深极浅，而蝴蝶不会沿直线飞行，它们会迅速飞出焦点范围。

2025013208.en_text: As well as thousands of attempts, it takes patience and fieldcraft to anticipate a butterfly’s likely flight-line — and catch it — in focus.
2025013208.cn_text: 除了数千次尝试，还需要耐心与野外技巧来预判蝴蝶可能的飞行路线，并在对焦状态下将其捕捉。

2025013209.en_text: So what’s the appeal of a long, sweaty day in pursuit of an elusive, fast-moving wild animal?
2025013209.cn_text: 那么，为追逐一种难以捉摸、快速移动的野生动物而度过漫长而汗流浃背的一天，吸引力何在？

2025013210.en_text: “It just feels bloody brilliant,” says Peters.
2025013210.cn_text: 「这感觉真是棒极了，」彼得斯说。

2025013211.en_text: “If I’ve had a full day of good encounters with butterflies, met interesting butterfly people and I’ve got some good shots, that becomes a vault in my spiritual bank.
2025013211.cn_text: 「如果我度过了充实的一天，与蝴蝶有过美好的邂逅，结识了有趣的蝴蝶爱好者，并拍到了一些精彩的照片，那就成为我精神银行中的一笔财富。

2025013213.en_text: A children’s author and poet who had become a keen amateur photographer, Peters watched the butterflies and idly wondered if he could capture them in flight.
2025013213.cn_text: 作为一名儿童作家和诗人，同时也是一位热衷的业余摄影师，彼得斯观察着蝴蝶，并随意地想知道自己能否捕捉到它们飞行的瞬间。

2025013214.en_text: It swiftly became an obsession as he recovered from a successful operation to remove the cancer.
2025013214.cn_text: 在成功接受癌症切除手术并康复期间，这迅速成为他的一种痴迷。

2025013215.en_text: In recent summers, he has travelled the length and breadth of Britain to photograph all 58 native species of butterfly.
2025013215.cn_text: 近几个夏天，他走遍英国各地，拍摄了全部58种本土蝴蝶物种。

2025013216.en_text: Now the fruits of those summers have been published in a beautiful new book.
2025013216.cn_text: 如今，那些夏日的成果已结集成一本精美的新书出版。

2025013217.en_text: A butterfly takes off so quickly it is still impossible to react quickly enough to capture that take-off but if he half-presses the shutter, the camera saves the 70 previous frames before the moment he actually takes the picture.
2025013217.cn_text: 蝴蝶起飞速度极快，人仍然无法反应得足够快来捕捉起飞瞬间，但若他半按快门，相机会保存他实际按下快门前的70帧画面。

2025013218.en_text: “It’s time travel, so I don’t miss the moment of take-off,” he says.
2025013218.cn_text: 「这就像时间旅行，所以我不会错过起飞的瞬间，」他说。

2025013219.en_text: After he’s captured the butterfly taking off, he layers 10 to 15 frames together in Photoshop.
2025013219.cn_text: 捕捉到蝴蝶起飞画面后，他会在Photoshop中将10到15帧画面叠加合成。

2025013220.en_text: Innovation and research have relied on public participation in science for centuries.
2025013220.cn_text: 几个世纪以来,创新与研究始终依赖公众对科学的参与。

2025013221.en_text: It was a musician who discovered the planet Uranus in the 18th century by making his own telescope with mirrors composed of copper and tin.
2025013221.cn_text: 18世纪时,一位音乐家用铜锡制作镜片自制望远镜,发现了天王星。

2025013222.en_text: Recent decades have seen science move into a convention where engagement in the subject can only be done through institutions, such as a university.
2025013222.cn_text: 近几十年来,科学已进入一种惯例,即只能通过大学等机构才能参与该学科。

2025013223.en_text: Citizen science provides an opportunity for greater public engagement and the democratisation of science.
2025013223.cn_text: 公民科学为更广泛的公众参与和科学民主化提供了机遇。

2025013224.en_text: In the information era, large data sets, small teams and financial restrictions have slowed scientific process.
2025013224.cn_text: 在信息时代,大规模数据集、小型团队和资金限制拖慢了科学进程。

2025013225.en_text: But by utilising the natural curiosity of the general public it is possible to overcome many of these challenges by engaging non-scientists directly in the research process.
2025013225.cn_text: 但通过利用公众与生俱来的好奇心,让非科学家直接参与研究过程,便可克服诸多此类挑战。

2025013226.en_text: Anyone can be a citizen scientist, regardless of age, nationality or academic experience.
2025013226.cn_text: 任何人都可以成为公民科学家,无论年龄、国籍或学术经历。

2025013227.en_text: You don’t even need any formal training, just an inquisitive mind and the enthusiasm to join one of the thousands of citizen science projects to generate new knowledge and the means to understand a genuine scientific outcome.
2025013227.cn_text: 你甚至无需任何正规培训,只需具备好奇之心和参与成千上万个公民科学项目的热情,即可产生新知识并理解真正的科学成果。

2025013228.en_text: Scientists have employed a variety of ways to engage the general public in their research, such as making data analysis into an online game or sample collection into a smartphone application.
2025013228.cn_text: 科学家采用了多种方式让公众参与其研究,例如将数据分析设计成在线游戏或将样本采集开发为智能手机应用。

2025013229.en_text: They’ve implored citizens to help with bug counting and categorising cancer cells, and even identifying distant galaxies.
2025013229.cn_text: 他们恳请公众协助统计昆虫数量、分类癌细胞,甚至识别遥远星系。

2025013230.en_text: This form of accessible science means that great minds are able to join the race to create and develop projects with the potential to change the world.
2025013230.cn_text: 这种开放式科学意味着优秀人才能够参与竞赛,创造并开发具有改变世界潜力的项目。

2025013231.en_text: A citizen science-based approach can extend the field of vision and include different ideas and different brains to problem-solve and create, making innovation faster and more effective.
2025013231.cn_text: 基于公民科学的方法可以拓展视野,纳入不同理念和不同智慧来解决问题并进行创造,从而使创新更快更有效。

2025013232.en_text: The rise of citizen science has grown alongside the rise of do-it-yourself biology laboratories around the world.
2025013232.cn_text: 公民科学的兴起与全球自助生物实验室的兴起同步发展。

2025013233.en_text: These groups of people are part of a rapidly expanding biotechnological social movement of citizen scientists and professional scientists seeking to take discovery out of institutions and put it into the hands of anyone with the enthusiasm.
2025013233.cn_text: 这些群体是一场迅速扩展的生物技术社会运动的组成部分,该运动由公民科学家和专业科学家构成,致力于将发现从机构中解放出来,交到任何有热情者手中。

2025013234.en_text: There are around 40 official do-it-yourself biology centres across the globe in locations including Paris, London, Sydney, and Tel Aviv.
2025013234.cn_text: 全球约有40个官方自助生物中心,分布于巴黎、伦敦、悉尼和特拉维夫等地。

2025013235.en_text: They pool resources, collaborate, think outside the box, and find solutions and ways around obstacles to explore science for the sake of science without the traditional boundaries of working inside a formal setting.
2025013235.cn_text: 他们集合资源、开展协作、突破思维定式、寻找解决方案和绕过障碍的途径,为科学而探索科学,不受正式机构工作的传统束缚。

2025013236.en_text: So is it time to take the Petri dish out of the laboratory and into the garage?
2025013236.cn_text: 那么,现在是否该将培养皿从实验室搬进车库了?

2026013001.en_text: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) are rapidly changing every aspect of human life.
2026013001.cn_text: 人工智能（AI）的进步正在迅速改变人类生活的各个方面。

2026013002.en_text: The world of AI is buzzing with an exciting potential to improve and enrich our lives.
2026013002.cn_text: 人工智能领域充满活力，蕴含着改善和丰富我们生活的巨大潜力。

2026013003.en_text: Still, AI also has the potential hazard of dominating our experiences in ways we might find difficult to control.
2026013003.cn_text: 然而，人工智能也存在潜在风险，可能以我们难以控制的方式主导我们的体验。

2026013004.en_text: One such area is how we understand and experience beauty.
2026013004.cn_text: 其中一个领域便是我们如何理解和体验美。

2026013005.en_text: AI can be a collaborative tool in a wide range of creative endeavors.
2026013005.cn_text: 人工智能可以成为广泛创意活动中的协作工具。

2026013006.en_text: Combining human creativity and AI algorithms can lead to unique artistic outcomes that are beautiful to the human eye.
2026013006.cn_text: 将人类创造力与人工智能算法相结合，可以产生人眼所见的独特艺术效果。

2026013007.en_text: These collaborations are likely to become increasingly common.
2026013007.cn_text: 这类合作可能会变得越来越普遍。

2026013008.en_text: For instance, as convenient and provocative, AI enables virtual try-on experiences where you can virtually test makeup, hairstyles, clothing, and even cosmetic procedures before making any physical changes.
2026013008.cn_text: 例如，人工智能提供便捷且富有启发性的虚拟试用体验，你可以在做出任何实际改变之前虚拟测试化妆品、发型、服装，甚至整容手术。

2026013009.en_text: Individuals can now experiment with different looks and explore their preferences, potentially expanding the range of beauty ideals.
2026013009.cn_text: 个人现在可以尝试不同的外观并探索自己的偏好，这可能拓宽美的标准范围。

2026013010.en_text: AI algorithms can analyze facial features and skin conditions to provide personalized beauty recommendations.
2026013010.cn_text: 人工智能算法可以分析面部特征和皮肤状况，从而提供个性化的美容建议。

2026013011.en_text: This customized approach aims to cater to individual preferences and enhance the concept of beauty tailored to each person’s unique characteristics.
2026013011.cn_text: 这种定制化方法旨在满足个人偏好，并提升根据每个人独特特征量身定制的美的理念。

2026013012.en_text: In this way, AI can be a fun vehicle for self-discovery.
2026013012.cn_text: 从这个意义上说，人工智能可以成为一种有趣的自我发现工具。

2026013013.en_text: While AI offers exciting possibilities, it also raises ethical concerns.There is a risk of deepening societal beauty pressures and perpetuating unattainable beauty standards.
2026013013.cn_text: 虽然人工智能提供了令人兴奋的可能性，但它也引发了伦理担忧。它可能加剧社会对美的压力，并延续难以企及的美的标准。

2026013014.en_text: Additionally, AIpowered beauty filters and editing tools can lead to distorted self-perception and contribute to body dissatisfaction.
2026013014.cn_text: 此外，人工智能驱动的美颜滤镜和编辑工具可能导致自我认知扭曲，并加剧身体不满情绪。

2026013015.en_text: As summarized in a recent post on “The Hidden Dangers of Online Beauty Filters”, relying on this technology for social presentation can cause harm such as body image issues, lower self-esteem, and social anxiety.
2026013015.cn_text: 正如最近一篇题为「在线美颜滤镜的隐患」的文章所总结的，依赖这种技术进行社交展示可能造成身体形象问题、自尊心下降和社交焦虑等危害。

2026013016.en_text: It’s important to note that while AI can enhance our appreciation of beauty, it should not replace the genuine human experience and the emotional connections we derive from seeing the beauty in each other.
2026013016.cn_text: 需要注意的是，虽然人工智能可以增进我们对美的欣赏，但它不应取代我们从彼此身上发现美所获得的真实人类体验和情感联系。

2026013017.en_text: For thousands of years, donkeys have been critical for propelling human civilizations forward.
2026013017.cn_text: 数千年来，驴在推动人类文明进程中发挥了关键作用。

2026013018.en_text: They’ve helped pull wheeled vehicles, carry travelers and move goods across the world.
2026013018.cn_text: 它们帮助拉动轮式车辆，运载旅行者，并在世界各地运输货物。

2026013019.en_text: But where and when these animals first became intertwined with humans has been a mystery.
2026013019.cn_text: 但这些动物最初在何时何地与人类发生联系一直是个谜。

2026013020.en_text: Now, researchers have used genomes of over 200 donkeys to trace their domestication back to a single event around 7,000 years ago in East Africa — about 3,000 years before humans tamed horses.
2026013020.cn_text: 如今，研究人员利用200多头驴的基因组，将其驯化追溯至约7000年前东非的一次单独事件——比人类驯服马早约3000年。

2026013021.en_text: The team published their findings in the journal Science this month.
2026013021.cn_text: 研究团队本月在《科学》期刊上发表了这一研究成果。

2026013022.en_text: “Through their DNA, the animals are telling their history themselves,” co-author Samantha Brooks, an equine researcher at the University of Florida, says in a statement.
2026013022.cn_text: 共同作者、佛罗里达大学马科动物研究员萨曼莎·布鲁克斯在一份声明中表示:「通过DNA，这些动物正在自己讲述它们的历史。」

2026013023.en_text: “We usually only get the human’s side of history through written accounts, but of course written history does not always record exactly how something happened.
2026013023.cn_text: 「我们通常只能通过书面记载了解人类一方的历史，但书面历史当然并不总能准确记录事件的真实经过。

2026013024.en_text: Looking at these DNA sequences, we get a biological testimony to the environment these animals lived in and the experiences they survived.”
2026013024.cn_text: 通过观察这些DNA序列，我们获得了关于这些动物所处生存环境及其经历的生物学证据。」

2026013025.en_text: The researchers examined 207 genomes from modern donkeys living in 31 countries across the globe.
2026013025.cn_text: 研究人员检测了来自全球31个国家现代驴的207个基因组。

2026013026.en_text: They also looked at genomes from 15 wild equids and 31 earlier donkeys that lived between about 4,000 and 100 years ago.
2026013026.cn_text: 他们还研究了15种野生马科动物以及31头生活在约4000年至100年前的早期驴的基因组。

2026013027.en_text: The team reconstructed the animals’ evolutionary tree and used computer models to pinpoint the domestication event when herders in Kenya and the Horn of Africa tamed wild asses.
2026013027.cn_text: 研究团队重建了这些动物的进化树，并利用计算机模型精确定位了肯尼亚和非洲之角的牧民驯化野驴的驯化事件。

2026013028.en_text: They then traced how the animals spread across the rest of the continent into Europe and Asia about 2,500 years later.
2026013028.cn_text: 随后他们追溯了这些动物如何在约2500年后扩散至非洲其他地区以及欧洲和亚洲。

2026013029.en_text: Though it’s still unclear why the original domestication happened, Science News’ Freda Kreier reports that the event coincided with the Sahara growing larger and drier.
2026013029.cn_text: 《科学新闻》记者弗雷达·克雷尔报道称，尽管最初驯化发生的原因仍不明确，但该事件恰好与撒哈拉沙漠的扩张及干旱化同时发生。

2026013030.en_text: “Donkeys are champions when it comes to carrying stuff and are good at going at deserts,” co-author Ludovic Orlando, an evolutionary biologist at Paul Sabin University in France, tells the publication.
2026013030.cn_text: 共同作者、法国保罗·萨班大学进化生物学家卢多维克·奥兰多向该刊物表示:「驴在运载物品方面是冠军，而且善于在沙漠中行进。」

2026013031.en_text: Prehistoric humans may have tamed donkeys to help navigate the expanding Sahara.
2026013031.cn_text: 史前人类可能驯化了驴，以便穿越不断扩张的撒哈拉沙漠。

2026013032.en_text: Researchers say these findings could help put donkeys in the spotlight.
2026013032.cn_text: 研究人员表示，这些发现可能有助于使驴受到更多关注。

2026013033.en_text: The animals could benefit from more research: Currently, there are no published genomes from donkeys located south of the Equator in Africa.
2026013033.cn_text: 这些动物可能受益于更多研究:目前尚无来自非洲赤道以南地区驴的已发表基因组。

2026013034.en_text: But understanding where the animals were first domesticated could guide archaeologists to a narrow region to search for insights about the original tamed donkeys.
2026013034.cn_text: 但了解这些动物最初被驯化的地点可以引导考古学家在特定区域搜寻有关最早被驯化驴的信息。

2026013035.en_text: Not only does understanding the equines’ genetic makeup help reveal their contribution to human history, but it also might improve their management in the future, as climate change alters the planet’s environment, write the authors.
2026013035.cn_text: 作者写道，了解这些马科动物的基因构成不仅有助于揭示它们对人类历史的贡献，还可能在气候变化改变地球环境之际改善未来对它们的管理。

2026013036.en_text: What can be learned about donkeys from Paragraph 1?
2026013036.cn_text: 从第一段可以了解到关于驴的哪些信息?

2026013037.en_text: They seemed mysterious to human ancestors.
2026013037.cn_text: 它们对人类祖先而言似乎神秘莫测。

2026013038.cn_text: 它们经历了多次驯化事件。

2026013039.en_text: They were tamed at an earlier time than horses.
2026013039.cn_text: 它们被驯化的时间早于马。

2026013040.en_text: They were vividly portrayed by ancient travelers.
2026013040.cn_text: 它们被古代旅行者生动地描述过。

2026013041.en_text: What message is conveyed in Brooks’ statement?
2026013041.cn_text: 布鲁克斯的陈述传达了什么信息?

2026013042.en_text: The earliest habitats of donkeys are hardly traceable.
2026013042.cn_text: 驴的最早栖息地几乎难以追溯。

2026013043.en_text: It is increasingly easy to read donkeys’ DNA sequences.
2026013043.cn_text: 读取驴的DNA序列变得越来越容易。

2026013044.en_text: Written accounts contain vital clues for donkey research.
2026013044.cn_text: 书面记载包含驴研究的重要线索。

2026013045.en_text: Genetic analysis offers insight into the history of donkeys.
2026013045.cn_text: 基因分析为驴的历史提供了深入了解。

2026013046.en_text: In their study, the researchers investigated how donkeys ____
2026013046.cn_text: 在研究中，研究人员调查了驴是如何____的。

2026013047.cn_text: 在世界范围内广泛传播

2026013048.en_text: survived with the help of herders.
2026013048.cn_text: 在牧民的帮助下存活下来

2026013051.cn_text: 关于驴最初被驯化的原因，奥兰多____

2026013053.cn_text: 提供了一种可能的解释

2026013054.en_text: calls for evidence from the Sahara.
2026013054.cn_text: 呼吁获取来自撒哈拉的证据

2026013055.en_text: holds a different view from Kreier.

2026013056.en_text: The authors think that their research could help with ____
2026013056.cn_text: 作者认为他们的研究可能有助于____

2026013057.cn_text: 加强对野生动物的保护

2026013060.cn_text: 提高人们对气候变化的认识

2026013061.en_text: There’s no business like show business — but in Los Angeles, it feels like there’s no business at all.
2026013061.cn_text: 没有什么行业比得上演艺业——但在洛杉矶,感觉如今根本就没有任何行业。

2026013062.en_text: If that sounds melodramatic, consider this: The Art Directors Guild, a labor union representing about 3,000 film workers, has suspended a training program and issued a statement explaining that “we cannot in good conscience encourage you to pursue our profession” This is a reaction to Hollywood’s decline, which is reaching a critical point for the industry and Southern California.
2026013062.cn_text: 如果这听起来过于夸张,不妨考虑以下事实:代表约3000名影视从业者的劳工组织艺术指导工会已暂停了一项培训计划,并发表声明解释称「我们无法昧着良心鼓励你们从事我们的职业」。这是对好莱坞衰退的反应,这种衰退正使该行业和南加州地区走到危急关头。

2026013063.en_text: Production has been slipping away from Hollywood since the 1950s, but the effects have never been more apparent than at present.
2026013063.cn_text: 自20世纪50年代以来,影视制作一直在从好莱坞流失,但这种影响从未像现在这样显著。

2026013064.en_text: Other regions in the United States, Canada and Europe have steadily increased incentives to attract TV shows and movies, leaving California in the dust.
2026013064.cn_text: 美国其他地区、加拿大和欧洲不断加大激励措施以吸引电视节目和电影拍摄,使加州相形见绌。

2026013065.en_text: Georgia offers up to 30% in transferable tax credits on film and TV production costs, plus an additional 10% increase on the base tax credit if the project includes a Georgia promotional logo.
2026013065.cn_text: 乔治亚州为影视制作成本提供高达30%的可转让税收抵免,如果项目中含有乔治亚州宣传标识,基础税收抵免还将额外增加10%。

2026013066.en_text: Even as California lost a huge volume of production to other locations, there was still plenty of film production taking place in Los Angeles before this year.
2026013066.cn_text: 尽管加州流失了大量制作业务到其他地区,但在今年之前,洛杉矶仍有大量影视制作活动。

2026013067.en_text: We were kept afloat by “peak TV” the glut of content that was required by the explosion of streaming services.
2026013067.cn_text: 我们依靠「巅峰电视时代」维持运转,即流媒体服务爆发式增长所需的海量内容。

2026013068.en_text: But 2022 was the peak of peak TV.
2026013068.cn_text: 但2022年是巅峰电视时代的顶峰。

2026013069.en_text: Back then platforms such as Netflix, Amazon and Apple TV hemorrhaged billions of dollars to generate content to attract new subscribers, resulting in 633 scripted series being released that year.
2026013069.cn_text: 当时Netflix、亚马逊和Apple TV等平台为吸引新订阅用户而大量烧钱制作内容,导致当年共上线了633部剧集。

2026013070.en_text: As the streamers’ emphasis changed from subscriber growth to profitability, prices for the services went up and the number of new shows went down to 481 released in 2023, with the number expected to dip into the 300s within a few years.
2026013070.cn_text: 随着流媒体平台的重心从用户增长转向盈利,服务价格上涨,新剧数量降至2023年的481部,预计几年内将降至300多部。

2026013071.en_text: If productions in Southern California dip below a critical level for too long, the industry’s essential talent will drift away along with enormous sums of revenue.
2026013071.cn_text: 如果南加州的影视制作长期跌破临界水平,该行业的核心人才将随巨额收入一同流失。

2026013072.en_text: Persuading studios to film here would become much more challenging if we couldn’t offer a deep bench of local film workers, on-screen talent and local businesses that support the entertainment industry.
2026013072.cn_text: 如果我们无法提供实力雄厚的本地影视从业者、荧幕人才以及支持娱乐产业的本地企业,说服制片厂在此拍摄将变得更加困难。

2026013073.en_text: That’s why the California Film Commission and its Los Angeles counterpart, Film LA, now should act, before it’s too late.
2026013073.cn_text: 这就是为什么加州电影委员会及其洛杉矶对口机构Film LA必须在为时已晚之前立即行动。

2026013074.en_text: These agencies and other government bodies should dramatically improve incentives to keep our current shows and attract new productions to Los Angeles.
2026013074.cn_text: 这些机构和其他政府部门应大幅改善激励措施,以留住现有剧集并吸引新制作来洛杉矶。

2026013075.en_text: Let’s go on with the show...and make sure the show doesn’t go on without us.
2026013075.cn_text: 让演出继续……并确保演出不会在没有我们的情况下继续。

2026013076.en_text: The Art Directors Guild’s statement reveals ____
2026013076.cn_text: 艺术指导工会的声明揭示了____

2026013077.cn_text: 人们对电影的兴趣减退。

2026013078.en_text: film workers’ nostalgia for the past.
2026013078.cn_text: 电影从业者对往昔的怀旧。

2026013081.en_text: The example of Georgia is used to illustrate the efforts to ____
2026013081.cn_text: 乔治亚州的例子用于说明____方面的努力。

2026013082.cn_text: 通过税收优惠吸引制作。

2026013085.en_text: collect funds for film and TV making.

2026013086.cn_text: 巅峰电视时代已过巅峰,因为____

2026013087.cn_text: 流媒体失去了技术优势。

2026013088.cn_text: 流媒体改变了战略重点。

2026013089.en_text: subscribers grew wary of large platforms.
2026013089.cn_text: 订阅用户对大型平台心存戒备。

2026013090.en_text: subscribers were unhappy with new shows.

2026013091.en_text: According to Paragraph 6, California’s entertainment industry might face ____
2026013091.cn_text: 根据第六段,加州娱乐产业可能面临____

2026013094.en_text: a brain drain to other places.

2026013101.en_text: The pioneers of wireless saw it as a gift to all the people.
2026013101.cn_text: 无线电的先驱们将其视为献给全人类的礼物。

2026013102.en_text: Sir John Reith said that it would end “isolation of the spirit” and rejoiced: “It does not matter how many thousands may be listening, there is always enough for others...the genius and the fool, the wealthy and the poor listen simultaneously.”
2026013102.cn_text: 约翰·里斯爵士说它将终结「精神上的孤立」，并欣喜地表示：「无论有多少千人在收听，总有足够的空间容纳他人……天才与愚者、富人与穷人同时聆听。」

2026013103.en_text: Between two great wars this technological innovation built a new kind of national consciousness.
2026013103.cn_text: 在两次世界大战之间，这项技术革新催生了一种新的国家意识。

2026013104.en_text: Opening this week, a book and exhibition curated by Beatty Rubens at the Bodleian in Oxford records how radio changed everyday life from 1922 to 1939.
2026013104.cn_text: 本周开幕，由比蒂·鲁本斯在牛津大学博德利图书馆策划的一本书和一场展览，记录了无线电如何在1922年至1939年间改变日常生活。

2026013105.en_text: She draws on letters, diaries and fiction, and a 1939 field notebook of verbatim audience research by Winifred Gill.
2026013105.cn_text: 她援引了书信、日记和小说，以及温妮弗雷德·吉尔1939年的一份逐字记录的受众研究田野笔记。

2026013106.en_text: There’s fun in testimonies of people enjoying the sheer newness.
2026013106.cn_text: 人们享受纯粹新奇感的证言中不乏趣味。

2026013107.en_text: A cartoon mocks a group failing to converse because they’re all in headphones.
2026013107.cn_text: 一幅漫画讽刺了一群人无法交谈，因为他们都戴着耳机。

2026013108.en_text: People report that broadcast music made workmen whistle new tunes.
2026013108.cn_text: 有人称广播音乐让工人们哼唱起新的曲调。

2026013109.en_text: A woman says there have been fewer street fights since the arrival of the wireless but also less stopping and “talking on the brush handle”.
2026013109.cn_text: 一位妇女说，自无线电出现以来，街头打斗减少了,但人们也不再停下来「倚着扫帚柄聊天」了。

2026013110.en_text: By and large the wireless was welcome.
2026013110.cn_text: 总体而言，无线电备受欢迎。

2026013111.en_text: I loved the man from the Thirties research who found that wireless suddenly offered “a lot of variety...things I thought I’d never be interested in...ice hockey perhaps”.
2026013111.cn_text: 我喜欢三十年代研究中那位男士的话，他发现无线电突然提供了「丰富多样的内容……一些我原以为自己永远不会感兴趣的东西……或许是冰球之类」。

2026013112.en_text: True: for more than 80 pre-digital years, linear speech broadcasting brought the gift of serendipity, random enlivening of a car journey or dull manual task.
2026013112.cn_text: 的确如此：在数字化之前的80多年里，线性语音广播带来了意外之喜，能够随机地为汽车旅程或枯燥的体力活增添生气。

2026013113.en_text: In my own book about radio I recorded how, on one drive: “I caught up with the news, learnt some 17thcentury history, and was startlingly educated by an unpretentious programme on the history of the stethoscope.”
2026013113.cn_text: 在我自己关于广播的书中，我记录了一次驾车经历：「我赶上了新闻，学到了一些17世纪的历史，还被一档朴实无华的听诊器历史节目出乎意料地教育了一番。」

2026013114.en_text: But radio’s enriching serendipity is ebbing.
2026013114.cn_text: 但广播那种丰富的意外之喜正在消退。

2026013115.en_text: With multiple networks and countless podcasts, a smartphone user selects what to hear and when.
2026013115.cn_text: 随着多个网络和无数播客的涌现，智能手机用户可以选择听什么以及何时听。

2026013116.en_text: And while it is wonderful to take a walk with anything in your headphones, infinite choice encourages us to shrink into niche interests and sympathetic beliefs.
2026013116.cn_text: 尽管戴着耳机散步可以听任何内容十分美妙，但无限的选择促使我们退缩到小众兴趣和志趣相投的信念中。

2026013117.en_text: A hundred years on from Marconi and Reith, is the art of mere listening endangered?
2026013117.cn_text: 马可尼和里斯的时代已过去一百年，单纯倾听的艺术是否正面临威胁？

2026013118.en_text: Some will say the audiobook boom revives it, though I suppose you can then worry about the decline of reading.
2026013118.cn_text: 有人会说有声书的繁荣让它得以复兴，尽管我想你随后又会担心阅读的衰落。

2026013119.en_text: But inventions shape all of us and it is worth noticing when techno-social habits do change, and asking whether to control them a bit or shield the youngest.
2026013119.cn_text: 但发明塑造着我们所有人，当技术社会习惯确实发生改变时，值得留意，并思考是否要稍加控制或保护年幼一代。

2026013120.en_text: Whatever we do, innovation will happen.
2026013120.cn_text: 无论我们做什么，创新都会发生。

2026013121.en_text: Today we fret about the isolating culture of smartphone-staring and selfievanity, but already in 1939 there was that lady regretting how, when all her street got wirelesses, it lost the neighbourly habit of “talking on the brush handle”.
2026013121.cn_text: 今天我们为盯着智能手机屏幕和自拍虚荣的孤立文化而忧虑，但早在1939年就有那位女士感慨，当她所在街区家家户户都装上无线电后，邻里间「倚着扫帚柄聊天」的习惯就消失了。

2026013122.en_text: It’s enough to make a person put down the smartphone and go out front with a yard broom.
2026013122.cn_text: 这足以让人放下智能手机，拿起院子扫帚走到门前。

2026013123.en_text: What can be learnt about wireless from Sir John Reith?
2026013123.cn_text: 从约翰·里斯爵士的话中可以了解到关于无线电的什么信息？

2026013124.cn_text: 它对所有人都是可及的。

2026013148.en_text: When Tom Swetnam joined the U.S. Forest Service in the 1970s, his mandate was to “put everything out,” he recalled.
2026013148.cn_text: 20世纪70年代汤姆·斯韦特纳姆加入美国林务局时，他的任务是「扑灭一切火情」，他回忆道。

2026013150.en_text: But when Swetnam enrolled in graduate school at the University of Arizona’s Laboratory of Tree-Ring Research, he was surprised to find a record of repeated blazes dating back hundreds of years before European colonists arrived on the continent.
2026013150.cn_text: 但当斯韦特纳姆在亚利桑那大学树轮研究实验室攻读研究生时，他惊讶地发现，在欧洲殖民者抵达美洲大陆之前的数百年间，曾发生过反复多次的火灾，均有记录在案。

2026013151.en_text: Some of the trees he analyzed bore more than 20 fire scars among their rings.
2026013151.cn_text: 他分析的一些树木，其年轮上有超过20处火灾疤痕。

2026013152.en_text: The fact that fires happened so often meant they couldn’t have been severe enough to kill most trees.
2026013152.cn_text: 火灾如此频繁发生这一事实意味着它们不可能严重到足以杀死大部分树木。

2026013153.en_text: Instead, a growing body of research showed that frequent, low-severity fires made many ecosystems healthier.
2026013153.cn_text: 相反，越来越多的研究表明，频繁发生的低烈度火灾使许多生态系统更加健康。

2026013154.en_text: They rid the forest of dead and sick trees, reducing competition and curbing the spread of disease.
2026013154.cn_text: 它们清除森林中的枯木和病树，减少了竞争并遏制了疾病传播。

2026013155.en_text: Because flammable material couldn’t build up on the landscape, blazes tended to move Slowly and peter out when they reached the footprints of previous burns.
2026013155.cn_text: 由于可燃物质无法在地表堆积，火势往往缓慢推进，并在抵达先前燃烧过的区域时自行熄灭。

2026013156.en_text: In 2022, Swetnam and other scientists teamed up to compile a database of fire-scarred trees from across the continent.
2026013156.cn_text: 2022年，斯韦特纳姆与其他科学家合作，编制了一个覆盖全美洲大陆的火灾疤痕树数据库。

2026013157.en_text: Their North American tree-ring fire-scar network (NAFSN) provided the basis for a study published last month.
2026013157.cn_text: 他们的北美树轮火疤网络（NAFSN）为上个月发表的一项研究提供了基础。

2026013158.en_text: In the study, the researchers compared the historical fire cadence with the wildfires recorded over the past few decades, and uncovered a striking shortfall.
2026013158.cn_text: 在该研究中，研究人员将历史火灾频率与过去几十年记录的野火进行对比，发现了一个显著的缺口。

2026013159.en_text: The NAFSN sites experienced less than a quarter of the number of fires that would have been expected without fire suppression.
2026013159.cn_text: NAFSN站点经历的火灾次数不到在没有火灾扑灭措施情况下预期次数的四分之一。

2026013160.en_text: This deficit is a testament to the effectiveness of modern firefighting, said Kelly Martin, a past president of the International Association of Wildland Fire.
2026013160.cn_text: 国际野火协会前主席凯利·马丁说，这一缺口证明了现代消防的有效性。

2026013161.en_text: “Yet the combined consequences of suppression and climate change have eroded humanity’s ability to suppress fires, particularly those that ignite under the most dangerous weather conditions.”
2026013161.cn_text: 「然而，火灾扑灭与气候变化的综合后果已削弱了人类扑灭火灾的能力，尤其是那些在最危险天气条件下引发的火灾。」

2026013162.en_text: To prevent entire ecosystems from going up in smoke, Martin said, people must bring healthy fire back to places that need it.
2026013162.cn_text: 马丁说，为了防止整个生态系统化为乌有，人们必须将有益的火带回需要它的地方。

2026013163.en_text: At Yosemite National Park, Martin oversaw the use of what is known as prescribed burns to make the landscape more resilient.
2026013163.cn_text: 在优胜美地国家公园，马丁监督使用所谓的计划性燃烧来增强地貌的韧性。

2026013164.en_text: These fires were carefully planned and intentionally ignited during periods when weather kept the blazes easy to control, and helped eliminate some of the fuel that had built up around the important park’s facilities.
2026013164.cn_text: 这些火灾经过周密规划，在天气条件便于控制火势的时期有意点燃，有助于清除公园重要设施周围积累的部分可燃物。

2026013165.en_text: Research shows that these prescribed burns make subsequent wildfires less severe, even if later fires happen under the most dangerous weather conditions.
2026013165.cn_text: 研究表明，这些计划性燃烧能降低后续野火的烈度，即使后来的火灾发生在最危险的天气条件下。

2026013166.en_text: Yet even as scientists and public officials increasingly agree on the need for more fires in our forests, climate change is making this tactic more challenging, experts said.
2026013166.cn_text: 专家表示，尽管科学家和政府官员日益认同森林需要更多火灾，但气候变化正使这一策略变得更具挑战性。

2026013167.en_text: “It’s a double-edged sword because wildfires are getting more severe and larger under climate change and we need this work even more, but then the work gets more challenging,” said Susan Prichard, a fire ecologist at the University of Washington.
2026013167.cn_text: 「这是一把双刃剑，因为在气候变化下野火变得更加严重、规模更大，我们更加需要这项工作，但与此同时这项工作也变得更具挑战性，」华盛顿大学火灾生态学家苏珊·普里查德说道。
